items.title: Maroc : le dirham dégringole, le déficit commercial atteint 25 milliards €
items.description: Déjà en butte à une situation économique et sociale délicate, les choses ne risquent pas de s’arranger de sitôt pour le Maroc qui enregistre une forte dépréciation de sa monnaie par rapport aux principales devises étrangères. La baisse de la valeur du dirham, conjuguée à la hausse des prix sur les marchés mondiaux, est susceptible d'alourdir la facture des importations et d’aggraver l’inflation. Maroc : le dirham dégringole face à l'euro et au dollar En un peu plus de deux mois, le dirham a perdu 3,9% de sa valeur. Il est passé de 10,76 dirhams pour un euro le 29 juillet dernier à 11,18 dirhams pour un euro le 6 octobre. C'est le plus haut niveau atteint par la monnaie unique européenne face au dirham marocain depuis mai 2018. Pendant la même période, la monnaie marocaine s'est encore davantage dépréciée par rapport au dollar, perdant 6,5% (9,38 à 9,99 dirhams pour un dollar entre fin juillet et début octobre). Il faut remonter à février 2025 pour retrouver un tel niveau bas du dirham marocain face au billet vert américain. La monnaie marocaine subit ainsi les contrecoups d’une situation mondiale tendue qui a fait flamber les prix de l'énergie et de nombreux produits et porté le dollar vers le haut, mais aussi de son propre système de change. Comme l’explique le journal marocain Médias 24, le dirham “évolue dans une bande de fluctuation de +5% autour d'un cours central fixé sur la base d'un panier composé à 60% de l'euro et à 40% du dollar”. Comme le dollar pèse 40% dans le panier de référence du dirham, son appréciation se répercute automatiquement sur le cours de la monnaie marocaine par rapport au billet vert américain. Maroc : la facture des importations en forte hausse La baisse du dirham face à l'euro s'explique, elle, par la forte hausse des importations qui accroît la demande de monnaie européenne pour régler les achats faits en euro. Si la baisse du dirham peut bénéficier à des secteurs comme le tourisme et certains secteurs exportateurs, elle demeure globalement négative pour une économie qui importe plus qu'elle n’exporte, comme l'explique au même média l’économiste marocain Omar Bakkou. Maroc : déficit commercial abyssal La facture des importations du royaume explose déjà. Selon le Haut-commissariat au plan (HCP), l'indice des valeurs unitaires à l'importation a augmenté de 10% au deuxième trimestre 2026, avec une très forte hausse (+53,1%) des prix des produits énergétiques importés. Selon l’Office des changes, le déficit commercial du Maroc s’est creusé de 25,4% à fin août 2026 pour atteindre 282,61 milliards de dirhams (25 milliards d’euros), contre 225,28 milliards un an auparavant. Les importations ont bondi de 15,8%, à 617,5 milliards de dirhams, tandis que les exportations n’ont augmenté que de 8,7%, à 334,89 milliards. Le tissu industriel et les consommateurs marocains se retrouvent ainsi doublement impactés par la conjugaison des effets de la hausse des prix à l’importation et de la baisse de la valeur de la monnaie locale. C'est le cocktail de l’inflation galopante. Le Maroc était l'un des pays les plus touchés par l’inflation mondiale qui avait suivi la crise sanitaire et le déclenchement de la guerre en Ukraine en 2022. Alors que le royaume multiplie les dépenses dans la politique de prestige, comme la construction de stades de football pour le Mondial 2030, sa population est écrasée par une crise sociale persistante, illustrée par les tentatives répétées de fuite collective de la jeunesse vers les enclaves espagnoles de Ceuta et Melilla. items.title: BoG cautions public against 20 unlicensed mobile loan apps
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has warned the public against using 20 mobile loan applications operating without its approval. The digital lenders are offering credit services without the required licence or authorisation from the central bank, the BoG said. In a notice, the Bank said the operations of the unlicensed providers contravened the Directive for Digital Credit Services Providers in Ghana and posed risks to users. The affected applications are Agile Loan, AmanaPay, CashWay, Foutou Credit, HastyCredit, InsCash, KudiNow, LendAura, Lever Credit, LoanGlide, NovaCedi, Palm Loan, PocketLoan, Rite Credit, SikaCare, SikaNow, Susu Loan, Taploan Up, Temivo Cedi and Zatuloan. The BoG said the operations raised concerns about customer data privacy, consumer protection and compliance with financial sector regulations. It urged the public to use only financial institutions and digital credit providers licensed and approved by the central bank. The Bank said it was working with relevant state agencies to identify, investigate and take enforcement action against unlicensed operators. It said the measures aimed to protect consumers and maintain the safety, integrity and stability of the financial sector.

items.title: Obi mourns Nafiu Baba-Ahmed, says Nigeria needs more voices for peace, justice
items.description: Former Anambra State Governor and 2023 Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has condoled with the family of Mallam Nafiu Baba-Ahmed, Secretary-General of the Supreme Council for Sharia in Nigeria, over his death. Obi disclosed this in a condolence message posted on his X platform on Wednesday. Describing Baba-Ahmed as a lawyer, scholar and administrator who served with dedication, Obi said the deceased was also a bridge-builder who believed in justice, peaceful coexistence and bringing people together. He said the death of Baba-Ahmed was a loss to his family, the Supreme Council for Sharia in Nigeria, Kaduna State, the Muslim Ummah and Nigeria. Obi said Baba-Ahmed’s death came at a time when the country needed more voices promoting peace, understanding and justice. “His passing is a loss to his family, the Council, Kaduna State, the Muslim Ummah and our nation. “At a time when Nigeria needs more voices for peace, understanding and justice, his absence will be deeply felt,” he said. Obi extended his condolences to Baba-Ahmed’s family, colleagues and others mourning his death. He prayed that Almighty God would forgive the deceased’s shortcomings, grant him eternal rest and give his loved ones the strength and comfort to bear the loss. items.title: 2027: Tinubu will win again if Atiku, Obi remain divided — Donald Duke
items.description: The presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, has predicted that President Bola Tinubu will win re-election in 2027 if leading opposition candidates fail to unite. Duke said the split opposition vote between Atiku Abubakar of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC) and Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), could repeat the outcome of the 2023 presidential election and give Tinubu an advantage. He spoke on Channels Television’s Morning Brief on Wednesday while discussing the chances of opposition candidates in the 2027 presidential election. Duke said the opposition would struggle to defeat the ruling party if major contenders continued to pursue separate presidential bids. “We don’t understand what we’re doing. If in the United States, which is the system we’ve largely just copied verbatim from, they have two major parties. If you fragmented the Democrats, for instance, into two or three other parties, the Republicans will remain in office forever. That’s what we’re doing,” he said. According to Duke, divisions among major opposition figures in 2023 spread votes among different candidates. “In 2023, we fragmented, and all the major opposition came from PDP. You had Vice President Atiku from the PDP. You had Peter, Labour at the time, and you had Kwankwaso. They fragmented,” he said. The former Cross River State governor attributed the difficulty of forging a common opposition platform partly to what he described as “large egos” among the leading contenders. He said the opposition figures appeared confident about their chances in 2027 but warned that they could be disappointed if they failed to work together. “These guys, the big ones you’re talking about, they’re preparing for inauguration. They think they’re going to win. I have news for them. They’re not going anywhere,” Duke said. He added that he did not see any of the leading opposition candidates emerging victorious if the opposition remained divided. “If I look at a crystal ball, what I see in that crystal ball is not them. I see another horror coming up,” he said. items.title: Gombe launches livestock vaccination against major diseases
items.description: …Jatau urges farmers, herders to embrace peace, veterinary services By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Government has commenced a statewide vaccination campaign against major livestock diseases, including Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia, CBPP, Foot and Mouth Disease, FMD, and Peste des Petits Ruminants, PPR. Flagging off the 2025/2026 vaccination exercise, the Deputy Governor, Dr Manassah Daniel Jatau, said the campaign was aimed at protecting livestock, safeguarding public health and strengthening the contribution of the livestock subsector to the state’s economy. Jatau, who represented Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya at the ceremony, said animal health was closely linked to human wellbeing and environmental health. He said diseases affecting livestock could have serious implications for human health, particularly through the consumption of animal products and close interaction between humans and animals. “Just as we emphasise the health of human beings, the health of the lower animals must also be considered and properly treated by human beings. “Healthy animals mean that human beings are interacting with disease-free animals. Healthy animals are a source of healthy meat that we consume, while healthy animals also have more value than diseased animals,” he said. The Deputy Governor said livestock remained a major source of livelihood, nutrition and employment for thousands of residents, while also providing milk, dairy products, animal traction and manure for agricultural activities. He added that livestock and their by-products were important to socio-cultural and religious practices, as well as the leather and tannery industries. Jatau said livestock production was also critical to Nigeria’s economic diversification efforts, noting that the subsector was a major employer of agricultural labour after crop farming. “Livestock production is a major employer of agricultural labour next to crop farming. Many people are engaged in livestock production, as well as the marketing of livestock and livestock products,” he said. State strengthens veterinary services The Deputy Governor said the state government had introduced several measures to strengthen veterinary services and livestock development. He said the government had established the Ministry of Livestock Development in line with the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda, while veterinary clinics across the state had also been renovated and equipped. Other interventions, he said, included the construction of a Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory, a solar-powered cold-chain facility and livestock training centres, as well as continuous statewide vaccination against animal diseases. Jatau also disclosed that work had commenced on a 184-hectare Special Livestock Development Zone, which he said would provide critical infrastructure for the livestock value chain. According to him, the facility will include an ultra-modern abattoir, tannery, international livestock market, veterinary hospital, poultry production unit and inland dry port. He said the project would reduce the risks and difficulties associated with transporting live animals to other parts of the country, while creating opportunities for livestock owners and other players in the value chain. “This is very important as it will save my cousins from carrying live animals to other parts of the country, in the midst of various inconveniences and sometimes accidents on the road,” Jatau said. He urged stakeholders to support the successful completion and sustainability of the project. Jatau urges farmers, herders to embrace peace The Deputy Governor also linked sustainable livestock development to peaceful relations between farmers and herders, saying the government was taking measures to address conflicts arising from agricultural and pastoral activities. He said the administration had constituted a Farmers-Herders Resolution Committee to promote peaceful coexistence, while efforts were also underway to re-demarcate and monument cattle routes and grazing reserves. According to him, the measures were intended to facilitate livestock movement, reduce farmers-herders clashes and create a conducive environment for agricultural and livestock production. “We need each other to live happily. At any rate, some of these animals belong to us, as some herders revealed to me,” he said. Jatau called on local government chairmen, traditional rulers, the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association, livestock owners, farmers and other stakeholders to support the government’s peacebuilding and livestock development initiatives. He particularly urged herders to use designated cattle routes where available and warned against moving livestock on major roads. “The continuous use of the main roads has led to the collapse of many roads, starting from the shoulders of the road. Of course, this creates maintenance costs to the government,” he said. The Deputy Governor also urged livestock owners and farmers to cooperate with veterinary personnel during the vaccination exercise, stressing that effective disease control required the collective efforts of government, livestock owners and communities. He expressed optimism that the campaign would improve animal health and livestock productivity while contributing to food security and better livelihoods across the state. Jatau subsequently declared the 2025/2026 statewide livestock vaccination campaign officially flagged off, describing it as part of the government’s efforts to improve animal health, protect human wellbeing and strengthen Gombe’s livestock economy. The post Gombe launches livestock vaccination against major diseases appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mahama urges tougher enforcement of building regulations over recent collapses
items.description: President John Mahama has called for tougher enforcement of building regulations at the district assembly level, following concerns over the recent collapse of buildings Speaking at the National Conference on Housing Finance on Wednesday, October 7, President Mahama said authorities must get to the root of building collapses and determine who is responsible for ensuring that buildings are safe. “Lately, you hear about collapsing buildings and all that. We must get to the roots of that, especially at the district assembly level,” he said. President Mahama explained that developers are required to obtain building permits from the relevant assemblies to ensure that their structures meet safety requirements. “When people are building, you are supposed to get a permit from the assembly to make sure that that building is safe,” he said. He, however, expressed concern about instances where developers continue construction despite being served with “stop work” orders. “More often than not, you see red paints, stop work, yet the work continues, and you wonder what is happening,” President Mahama noted. President Mahama therefore tasked the Ministry of Local Government with taking the issue seriously and ensuring accountability when buildings collapse. “These are things that the Ministry of Local Government should take very seriously. If a house collapses, we must see whose duty it was to ensure that that house was safe. And that person must be sanctioned for it,” he said. The President also turned to the challenge of housing affordability, stressing that housing policy succeeds only if ordinary Ghanaians can afford the homes being delivered. “A housing policy succeeds when people can afford to live in the homes that it delivers, and affordability lies at the heart of our housing challenge,” he said. He noted that the problem is not necessarily a lack of housing construction, but that many of the houses being delivered remain beyond the financial reach of the average Ghanaian. “It is not like houses are not being delivered. But the kinds of houses that are being delivered are way beyond the reach of the average Ghanaian,” President Mahama stated. He said high borrowing costs, substantial deposits and short repayment periods continue to make home ownership difficult for many households. President Mahama called for financing arrangements that reflect the realities of Ghanaian incomes, including longer-term financing in local currency, manageable repayments and clear terms that households can understand. He further highlighted the role of the National Home Ownership Fund in expanding access to housing finance. According to him, partnerships with GCB Bank, Stanbic Bank and Republic Bank have supported government-backed mortgage facilities and rent-to-own arrangements. He said the interventions have helped more than 1,000 people to own homes, while the City Mortgage rate under the National Mortgage Scheme currently stands at 8.4 per cent. “This is a good start, and I commend the Board of Management and partner institutions for this progress,” he said.

items.title: 3 ans après le "7 Octobre", Guterres alerte sur l'enfer persistant à Gaza
items.description: Au triste 3è anniversaire des attaques du 7 octobre 2023, le Secrétaire général des Nations Unies, Antonio Guterres, a lancé un appel solennel pour mettre fin au calvaire de la population palestinienne dans la bande de Gaza. Tout en condamnant à nouveau l'offensive initiale du Hamas, le chef de l'ONU a braqué les projecteurs sur la tragédie humanitaire et les destructions sans précédent infligées à l'enclave palestinienne au cours des trois dernières années. Le bilan de la riposte militaire israélienne à Gaza demeure vertigineux : plus de 74 000 morts, selon les données du ministère de la Santé local, et une enclave dévastée où plus de 80% des infrastructures ont été détruites, laissant derrière elles quelque 61 millions de tonnes de décombres. Bien qu'un accord de cessez-le-feu ait été instauré le 10 octobre 2025 sous le parrainage de l'administration américaine, permettant la libération des derniers captifs, les frappes israéliennes n'ont jamais totalement cessé, coûtant la vie à au moins 1 358 Palestiniens supplémentaires depuis l'entrée en vigueur de la trêve. Un an après l'arrêt officiel des combats majeurs, la situation sur le terrain reste critique. La reconstruction est au point mort et plus d'un million de déplacés s'entassent dans des campements de fortune précaires, tandis que deux millions d'habitants demeurent confinés sur à peine un tiers du territoire gazaoui. Un rapport du 'Conseil de la paix' évalue les dommages matériels directs à 35,2 milliards de dollars, et le coût global de la reconstruction sur la prochaine décennie à plus de 71,4 milliards de dollars. Face à ce « jour d'après » au point mort et au blocage des phases ultérieures du plan de paix qui devaient organiser le retrait des forces d'occupation, la gouvernance et l'acheminement massif de l'aide, Guterres a insisté qu'un cessez-le-feu précaire ne pouvait se substituer à un règlement politique durable. Il a en ce sens appelé à la levée des entraves humanitaires, au respect strict du droit international et à la concrétisation de la solution à deux États, seule voie à même de garantir dignité, sécurité et justice aux peuples palestinien et israélien. The post 3 ans après le "7 Octobre", Guterres alerte sur l'enfer persistant à Gaza appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: FWSC denies reports of salary deductions for striking teachers
items.description: The Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) has denied media reports suggesting that its Chief Executive, Dr George Smith-Graham, said teachers participating in the ongoing strike would have their salaries deducted for every day they remain away from work. The Commission said Dr Smith-Graham did not make the comments attributed to him and urged the public and the media to disregard the reports and any conclusions drawn from them. In a statement signed by the Head of Public Affairs of the FWSC, Emelia Ennin, the Commission said the purported comments do not represent the position of either the Chief Executive or the Commission on the ongoing industrial action by the three pre-tertiary teacher unions. “The Fair Wages and Salaries Commission wishes to state that our Chief Executive did not make the comments attributed to him in the said media report,” the statement said. “The FWSC therefore respectfully appeals to the public and the media to disregard the purported comments and any conclusions drawn from them, as they do not represent a statement made by the Chief Executive or a position taken by the Commission in relation to the ongoing teachers’ strike.” The Commission said its current engagement with the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) is focused on dialogue and negotiations to address outstanding issues relating to their collective agreement and conditions of service. The FWSC said it engaged the leadership of the three unions on Tuesday, October 6, as part of efforts to resolve the issues underlying the industrial action. The meeting was chaired by Dr Smith-Graham and attended by GNAT General Secretary Thomas Musah, NAGRAT President Jacob Anaba, PRETAG President King Awudu Ali and other leaders of the unions. According to the Commission, the meeting provided an opportunity for both sides to discuss the outstanding issues and demands raised by the unions. Speaking after the meeting, Dr Smith-Graham said the engagement would be reconvened at a later date to allow the Commission to undertake further consultations on the demands presented by the unions and engage relevant stakeholders before negotiations resume. He also commended the union leaders for the peaceful manner in which the meeting was conducted. The engagement forms part of the formal process initiated by government to address the concerns of the three teacher unions following the commencement of their nationwide strike on Monday, September 28. The FWSC’s involvement followed an emergency meeting convened by the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, with the leadership of the three unions on September 28, after the strike began. The Minister subsequently indicated that the FWSC would spearhead the next phase of formal negotiations on behalf of the government. The Commission said it remains committed to constructive engagement with the teacher unions and other relevant stakeholders towards finding a mutually acceptable and sustainable resolution to the outstanding issues. “The Commission acknowledges the importance of the concerns raised by the unions and believes that continued dialogue and good-faith negotiations remain critical to resolving the issues,” it said. The FWSC has therefore urged the public, the media and other stakeholders to rely on verified information from the Commission and other appropriate authorities for updates on the negotiations. It reiterated its commitment to promoting fair, transparent and sustainable compensation arrangements while fostering harmonious industrial relations in Ghana’s public service.

items.title: Carvajal deal has broken down, says Getafe president
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Getafe president Ángel Torres has retracted his earlier comments suggesting former Real Madrid captain Dani Carvajal was close to joining the LaLiga club, saying the proposed deal has now broken down. According to ESPN, Torres had previously told DAZN that Getafe were working on a deal for the 34-year-old defender, who has been without a club since his Real Madrid contract expired in June. “We’re working on it. He has passed a medical and everything. All that is missing is for LaLiga and me to reach an agreement,” Torres had said. However, when asked about Carvajal’s possible arrival on Wednesday, Torres changed his position, saying: “There’s nothing, [the agreement] has broken down.” Carvajal, a Real Madrid academy graduate, spent 13 seasons with the club and won 27 trophies, including six Champions League titles, a joint-record tally. The Spain international’s later years at the Santiago Bernabéu were disrupted by serious injuries. He suffered a cruciate ligament tear in October 2024 and another significant knee injury a year later, limiting him to 23 appearances for Real Madrid last season. items.title: Rooted like a tree, responsive like a river: Dr Amin Adam calls for new model of Imamship to meet modern realities
items.description: Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has called for a new model of Islamic leadership to meet Ghana’s fast-changing social realities, arguing that Imams must remain spiritually grounded while adapting their tools and institutions. Speaking at the 5th National Conference of Regional Imams in Accra, Dr Amin Adam said the central question facing the Muslim community today was how the Imam could continue to lead effectively without losing his trusted authority. “How does the Imam in modern times continue to lead a community whose needs, pleasures and expectations are changing faster than at any time in our history without losing the spiritual authority and the traditions that have made him trusted for generations?” he posed. “My answer this afternoon is this: the Imam of today and the future must be rooted like a tree and responsive like a river,” he told the gathering of regional Imams, scholars and Zongo leaders. Explaining his metaphor, the former minister said resilience was about combining doctrinal roots with modern responsiveness. “What it means in our context is that the Imam must be rooted in the Quran and the Sunnah but responsive in the methods, institutions and the tools that he uses to serve. This combination is what we need to produce resilient Imams,” he stressed. Dr Amin Adam traced the historic role of Imams in Ghana, noting that from the old scholarly centres of Wa, Dagbon and Salaga to the Zongos of Accra, Kumasi, Takoradi and Koforidua, the Imam had never been only the person who led the five daily prayers. “In Ghana, the Imam has been a teacher, a judge of family disputes, a marriage officiant, a counsellor, a mediator, an adviser to chiefs and the voice of the community before the authorities,” he said. He added that the need for resilient leadership was even more urgent given the size and youthfulness of Ghana’s Muslim population. “Today, Muslims make up roughly one in every five Ghanaians. That is about twenty per cent, according to the 2021 Population and Housing Census. But I believe we are more than this. That is several million citizens whose spiritual life, family stability, social welfare and increasingly economic prospects depend heavily on the quality of their local Imam,” he added. The conference, which brought together Regional Chief Imams from across the 16 regions and other Islamic leaders, is expected to deliberate on the training, welfare and standardisation of Imamship in Ghana.

items.title: La Traditional Council secures suspension of SSNIT’s La Pleasure Beach redevelopment plans
items.description: The La Traditional Council says plans by the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) to redevelop the demolished La Pleasure Beach Resort have been suspended pending further consultations among key stakeholders. The development follows a high-level meeting involving SSNIT, the management of Labadi Beach Hotel, the Minister for Local Government, the Greater Accra Regional Minister and other relevant stakeholders. The meeting was convened amid concerns from the La Traditional Council over the demolition of the facility and what it considers a failure by the authorities to adequately consult the traditional leadership before the exercise. Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, October 7, the La Shikitele, Nii Adjei Koofeh IV, said the Traditional Council expressed its strong dissatisfaction with the manner in which the demolition was conducted. “What we said at the meeting was that, firstly, we were very aggrieved and unhappy about the approach because we were not engaged and involved,” he said. According to him, the Council should have been consulted before the demolition because it considers itself a key stakeholder in matters concerning the land on which the facility was situated. “National Security said it is not every operation or exercise that people need to know. We told them that we are primary stakeholders as the landowners,” he added. SSNIT, National Security apologise Nii Adjei Koofeh IV disclosed that both SSNIT and National Security subsequently apologised to the Traditional Council for failing to engage it before the demolition. He said the parties had now agreed that further steps concerning the site should follow due process and involve the relevant stakeholders. “The National Security also apologized for not engaging us before the exercise was carried out. On the way forward, they said they want everything to be done according to due process and proper arrangements. So the intended redevelopment that SNIT wants to start should be put on hold. “Now they are going to form a committee to go into the issues and then consider the plans that SSNIT has for the place for us to come to an amicable settlement that will lead to the satisfaction of all stakeholders,” he said. The suspension means SSNIT’s proposed redevelopment of the former La Pleasure Beach site will not proceed immediately, as a committee is expected to examine the concerns raised by the Traditional Council and review the Trust’s plans for the property. The Council says the committee’s work should provide an opportunity for all parties to resolve their differences and reach an arrangement acceptable to the various stakeholders. La Council demands protection for indigenes Beyond the dispute over the demolition and redevelopment plans, the La Traditional Council is also insisting that the interests of the La community be taken into consideration in any future agreement concerning the site. In particular, the Council wants the interests of La indigenes who were employed at the facility to be protected as discussions on the future of the property continue. The Council maintains that any redevelopment arrangement should take account of its interests as the traditional authority and landowner, while also considering the livelihoods and employment of members of the La community affected by developments at the site.

items.title: Joy FM listeners support mother seeking treatment for 3-year-old daughter after alleged sexual abuse
items.description: A mother who feared for the life of her three-year-old daughter has received financial support from listeners of Joy FM’s Joy Time in His Presence after sharing her distressing situation on air. The revamped early-morning Christian prayer, worship and devotional programme not only exhorts listeners but also prays with them and ministers to their needs and concerns. The mother, who cannot be named, reached out to the programme during its phone-in session to seek prayers and assistance to secure medical care for her daughter. According to Abigail, her daughter had allegedly been sexually abused and was subsequently taken seriously ill. She said the child was exuding a foul smell and described her condition as so bad that she feared she was “dying”. With no money to take the child to hospital, Abigail turned to Joy Time in His Presence for help. The account left host Ps. Ato Acquah deeply moved. He immediately prayed with Abigail, asking God to intervene and bring healing to her young daughter. Listeners also responded with financial support. Before the programme ended, Abigail sent another message to the show, thanking the team and listeners for their support. She said some money had been raised to help her begin treatment for her daughter. For a mother who had reached out in desperation, the assistance offered by listeners provided some relief and, more importantly, hope that her daughter could receive the care she needed. JoyNews follows up JoyNews is following up on the case and working to ensure that the appropriate authorities, including the police, are brought in. The aim is to help secure the necessary intervention for the child and ensure that those responsible for the alleged abuse are identified and, where appropriate, brought to justice. The case is also a painful reminder of the dangers children face and the need for adults to take reports of abuse seriously and act quickly. Joy Time in His Presence The incident is one of several moments in which Joy Time in His Presence has provided a platform for listeners to share personal challenges and seek prayer and support. The weekday devotional programme, which airs on Joy FM from 4:00am to 5:45 am, has recently placed greater emphasis on the needs and concerns of its listeners. Through phone-ins and WhatsApp messages, listeners are given the opportunity to talk about issues affecting their lives and receive prayers from the programme. For Abigail, one WhatsApp message became a cry for help. Before the programme ended that morning, help had begun to come. Joy Time in His Presence airs weekdays on Joy FM from 4:00 am to 5:45 am.

items.title: German Unity Day celebrated with music, art and Ghana-Germany friendship in Accra
items.description: The German Embassy in Accra marked German Unity Day on September 30 with a festival celebrating the friendship and partnership between Ghana and Germany. The event brought together music, dance, art and cultural performances, with Guy Bertrand opening the evening with the national anthems. The Universal Street Academy followed with a performance, while the Patchbay Band and Daakyehemaa provided musical entertainment. Ghanaian music legend Okyeame Kwame also performed before DopeNation took guests through a high-energy set that turned the German residence into a dance floor. Musician KiDi also made a special appearance at the celebration. The event also featured an art exhibition by Accra-based German artist Rebekka Macht, who presented works from her latest series exploring care and humanity’s connection with nature. The celebration was attended by Defence Minister Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, who represented the Government of Ghana as special guest, alongside Education Minister Harouna Iddrisu and Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin. Beyond the festivities, the celebration highlighted the importance of unity and the longstanding relationship between Ghana and Germany. German Unity Day commemorates the reunification of Germany following the fall of the Berlin Wall and the subsequent reunification of East and West Germany. The celebration in Accra drew parallels between Germany’s experience of overcoming division and Ghana’s ability to maintain national cohesion despite its diversity. The German Embassy described Ghana and Germany as two democracies and middle powers committed to international cooperation, rules-based relations and taking responsibility within their respective regions. The bilateral partnership currently focuses on areas including security, investment and value creation, skills development and climate action. The celebration also looked ahead to major engagements between the two countries, including the German-African Business Summit scheduled to take place in Accra in November and a planned second visit to Ghana within a year by German Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. The September 30 celebration therefore served not only as a commemoration of German Unity Day but also as a cultural expression of the growing people-to-people ties between Ghana and Germany. The event underscored the importance of building trust and stronger connections between the two countries, with culture and shared experiences providing a platform for deepening the partnership.

items.title: MEHSOG and GFD build capacity of Ashanti Region journalists on inclusive disability reporting
items.description: The Mental Health Society of Ghana (MEHSOG) and the Ghana Federation of Disability Organisations (GFD) have held a media capacity-building workshop aimed at promoting effective and inclusive reporting on disability. The workshop, supported by the Ashanti Regional branch of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), was held under the theme “Effective Media Reporting on Disability: Promoting Economic Justice and Inclusion through Responsible Journalism.” It forms part of the project “Strengthening the Capacity of Organisations of Persons with Disabilities for Promoting Inclusion in Ghana,” which is funded by the European Union. The Executive Director of the Ghana Federation of Disability Organisations (GFD), Peter Anomah-Kordieh, underscored the critical role of the media in advancing the welfare and rights of persons with disabilities. According to him, the media remains a strategic partner in advocating for inclusion, as it helps to amplify the concerns of persons with disabilities and educate the public on the need to remove barriers that hinder their full participation in society. “The media plays a very critical role in our work. They amplify the issues of persons with disabilities in the country, so we always encourage and partner with them to project our issues,” he said. He explained that such partnerships are essential to highlight pressing challenges, including the high number of persons with disabilities who remain out of school, face discrimination in the job market, or struggle to access inclusive and accessible health services. Mr. Anomah-Kordieh noted that sensitising employers, health facilities and other public institutions on disability inclusion is crucial to achieving economic justice and equal opportunities. He said while the media generally reports with good intentions, the inappropriate use of language often undermines the dignity of persons with disabilities. He explained that person-first language has become the global standard in disability reporting. Terms like “disabled people” or “disabled person” are discouraged because they define individuals solely by their disability, while “persons with disabilities” is preferred because it recognises their humanity first. “We are human beings first before our disability, so we prefer to be called ‘persons with disabilities’,” he said. He further clarified that the phrase “persons living with disabilities” is inaccurate because disability is not a disease or medical condition one lives with, and that the use of “normal people” to describe persons without disabilities is inappropriate because it implies persons with disabilities are abnormal. He therefore urged journalists to be more conscious of their choice of words and to adopt inclusive, respectful and dignified terminologies in their reportage. The workshop was structured to deliver six key outputs, including deepening understanding of rights-based and disability-inclusive reporting, encouraging the use of appropriate disability terminology, and highlighting economic justice concerns affecting persons with disabilities. It was also expected to provide participants with a practical understanding of the Guidelines for Media Reporting on Disability in Ghana. Addressing participants, the Chairman of the Ashanti Regional Ghana Journalists Association, Mr. Kofi Adu Domfeh, said the training was crucial to move the conversation on inclusion from rhetoric to practical action. He noted that the media has the power to either reinforce negative stereotypes about persons with disabilities or to challenge them by highlighting their dignity, abilities and contributions to society. The Chairman of the Ashanti GJA observed that disability is often portrayed through charity, vulnerability and dependency, rather than from a rights-based perspective that focuses on opportunity, participation and equal citizenship, underscoring the need for a paradigm shift. He urged journalists to be more intentional about inclusivity, including in policy reporting, and to ensure that persons with disabilities are featured not just as subjects but as active voices and expert sources in stories that affect them. “The Ghana Journalists Association therefore encourages media practitioners to give greater visibility to the voices and experiences of persons with disabilities. We must ensure that they are not merely subjects of stories, but active participants in the conversations that affect their lives,” Mr Domfeh emphasised. He said the workshop offers an opportunity for journalists to re-examine their language choices, adopt person-first and rights-based terminologies, and ensure that media coverage promotes dignity, respect and inclusion for all. He therefore called on disability organisations to strengthen their engagement with the media by providing credible data, compelling human-interest stories and access to their members. “This also requires building the capacity of journalists to report disability issues responsibly. We need more accurate, inclusive and solutions-oriented reporting that examines barriers to education, employment, healthcare, political participation, accessibility and economic empowerment” He pledged the commitment of the Ashanti GJA to working with relevant stakeholders to promote journalism that advances inclusion, dignity and social justice. Mr. Domfeh said the Association will continue to collaborate with disability organisations, civil society and development partners to ensure that media practice in the region contributes to building an inclusive society where no one is left behind. A Senior Lecturer at the Department of Health Promotion, Education and Disability Studies at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Dr. Enoch Acheampong, led a session on participation barriers, focusing on health and social inclusion. He said persons with disabilities continue to face significant communication, attitudinal and physical barriers that hinder their access to healthcare, education and public infrastructure. According to him, many health facilities in the country are not disability-friendly, leaving persons with disabilities to struggle to access essential services. “When you go to the hospital with your condition, there is often a communication barrier between you and the health practitioner. For instance, if you are deaf, how do you communicate when there is no sign language interpreter available?” he asked. He cited the example of visually impaired persons who are unable to read handwritten dosage instructions, such as 0-0-0 or 1-0-1, commonly written on drug envelopes, a situation he said could have serious health implications. “As a country, we need to take a critical look at our healthcare system. The communication barriers and physical barriers that persons with disabilities face must be addressed,” he said. Dr. Acheampong further noted that inaccessible physical infrastructure, including buildings without ramps and information not available in accessible formats, continues to exclude persons with disabilities from full participation in society. He also addressed harmful misconceptions about the sexuality and reproductive rights of persons with disabilities, including the false belief that they are asexual or incapable of having relationships. He said such misconceptions not only deny persons with disabilities their right to love, marriage and family life but also contribute to their exclusion from sexual and reproductive health information and services. He therefore urged journalists to use their platforms to help demystify these misconceptions, challenge stigma and educate the public on the rights of persons with disabilities to marriage, family life and full social inclusion. Organisers and facilitators of the training expressed optimism that the workshop will enhance accurate, inclusive and solutions-oriented reporting on disability issues in Ghana. They noted that equipping journalists with the right knowledge and terminologies will help challenge stereotypes and improve the quality of reportage, while deepening collaboration between the media and disability organisations to advance economic justice and full inclusion.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi, Indian opposition lawmakers detained over election chief protest for 2nd day
items.description: Indian police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two days on Wednesday as they launched an unannounced protest demanding the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists. Opposition parties, their student units, and the “ cockroach ” youth movement have been staging almost daily demonstrations seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, after the Indian Express newspaper last month reported disagreements within the poll panel over updating voter lists, stoking concerns over its neutrality. Opposition lawmakers led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi protested on Tuesday as well, seeking a meeting with Kumar and his deputies, before police broke up their gathering and briefly detained them. Wednesday’s protest began after a lunch meeting of lawmakers that Congress organised at a restaurant in central Delhi, close to the Jantar Mantar site where authorities permit demonstrations. “Yesterday … Delhi Police stopped us and said you cannot protest here … so today … we will go to the designated protest site, sit there, and tell the country that, for us, Gyanesh Kumar is not the legitimate commissioner,” Gandhi told reporters, referring to Jantar Mantar. “The people who have done this (vote theft) are traitors … Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign,” he said, before boarding a bus that was to take the lawmakers to Jantar Mantar. New political challenge to Modi Lawmakers in the bus held posters against the windows that said, “no vote theft, no democracy theft”, and “election commission, not BJP commission”, referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party. Hundreds of Congress members accompanied the bus on foot amid heavy deployment of police and paramilitary personnel in riot gear. Police also closed the road leading to Jantar Mantar, forcing the bus to take a detour. Gandhi later stepped out of the bus, with a live feed on his party’s YouTube channel showing him standing at the centre of a crowd of protesters and security personnel, while his sister Priyanka Vadra and other lawmakers sprawled out on the road. India’s Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi (centre, L) scuffles with a policeman during a protest by the opposition alliance INDIA bloc in New Delhi on October 7, 2026 against the country’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, calling for his resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. — AFP Visuals showed security personnel hauling Gandhi and Vadra into separate vehicles and taking them away. There was no immediate comment from the police on the detentions. The demonstrations present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term, just months after similar protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) youth movement forced the resignation of his education minister over exam paper leaks. Kumar has not commented on the voter lists issue but the election commission and BJP have denied accusations of wrongdoing.

items.title: A woman should not have to choose between being fed and being safe
items.description: The first time her husband slapped her, Esi called her mother. “What happened?” her mother asked. Esi explained. Then came a long silence. “Does he still give you housekeeping money?” She looked at the phone, wondering whether her mother had heard her. “Yes.” “Then calm down. We will talk to him.” The second time, he pushed her against the wardrobe. The next morning, he transferred money for the children’s school fees and sent her a message. Paid. Confirm receipt. She typed, Received, thank you. She deleted the thank you before sending. At Sunday lunch, her aunt admired the new car parked outside. “Your husband really takes care of you.” Esi pulled her sleeve over the bruises on her wrist. “He hurt me, Auntie.” Her aunt lowered her voice. “My dear, some women don’t even get chop money. You have to consider everything.” So Esi began considering everything. The rent. The school fees. The groceries. The way her daughter stopped chewing whenever Daddy’s car entered the compound. The way her son had started saying, “You made me do it,” whenever he hit his little sister. One evening, her husband threw a plate because the stew was cold. Their daughter helped Esi pick up the pieces after he went upstairs. “Mummy,” she whispered, “when I grow up, I’ll buy you a house.” Esi’s hand stopped over a broken piece. “Why?” “So nobody can sack you when they’re angry.” That night, Esi called her sister. This time, she told the whole story. Together, they began arranging somewhere she and the children could stay. When her mother heard, she asked the familiar question. “But who will take care of you?” “I need you to ask whether we are safe first.” For once, her mother had no answer ready. A week later, Esi stood at her sister’s kitchen sink, washing the children’s breakfast bowls. The tap leaked. There was no microwave, and three of them were sharing one room. Behind her, her daughter spilled a cup of milk. The child froze. Esi handed her a cloth. “Wipe it, sweetheart.” “Are you angry?” “No. It’s only milk.” Her daughter smiled and reached for the cloth. Esi turned back to the sink and cried quietly. She still needed money. There were fees to pay and a life to rebuild. She knew exactly what money could do. What she could no longer understand was why everyone kept asking it to explain a slap. Before You Ask What She Did “What she could no longer understand was why everyone kept asking money to explain a slap.” That was where we left Esi: standing at her sister’s kitchen sink, discovering that her daughter could spill milk without anyone shouting, threatening or reaching for something to throw. But leaving the house did not end the questions. “Have you thought about the children?” “Can’t your family speak to him?” “Are you going to leave your marriage over this?” Few people asked how long she had been afraid in her own home. Even fewer asked why the children had learnt to recognise danger from the sound of their father’s car. For many women, speaking about abuse means preparing to defend themselves before anyone offers them comfort. In some African homes, a woman can gather the courage to tell her parents that her husband has beaten her, only to hear: “What did you do to provoke him?” Did you talk back? Did you disrespect him? Was his food ready? Why didn’t you keep quiet when you saw that he was angry? Before anyone asks where she is hurt, they ask what she did. That question carries a message a daughter may never forget: there might be an acceptable reason for someone to beat her, and her first responsibility is to prove she did not supply it. Of course, African families are not all the same. There are parents who protect their daughters, challenge abusive husbands and offer a place to return without humiliation. But where silence, endurance and family reputation take priority, a woman may discover that the people she hoped would protect her are more concerned about keeping her married. We need to be honest about what that does to her. The next time it happens, she may not call. She may cover the bruise, cancel a visit or say she fell. She may begin rehearsing her words before every conversation with her husband, trying to find the version of herself that will never upset him. When people keep asking what she did to provoke him, she can start asking herself the same thing. Perhaps I should have waited. Perhaps my tone was wrong. Perhaps I should have kept quiet. There can be disagreements in a marriage. People can speak carelessly, hurt each other’s feelings and owe each other apologies. None of that gives either partner permission to use violence. A husband remains responsible for choosing to hit his wife. Yet we often place the burden of preventing his next attack on her. Then money enters the conversation. “But he provides.” He pays the rent. The children attend good schools. There is food in the house. From outside, the family looks comfortable, and that comfort becomes evidence people use to question her pain. We are gradually making money look silly by asking it to do work it cannot do. We ask what he pays for, as though that answers what he has done. Money can pay a hospital bill. It cannot make the injury acceptable. It can buy a beautiful bed. It cannot give a woman restful sleep beside someone she fears. It can pay school fees. It cannot erase what children learn when they watch one parent terrorise the other. Financial provision matters. Anyone who has struggled to feed a family knows that. It can also make leaving painfully difficult when a woman has no income, no savings and nowhere safe to go. But provision should never become permission. A woman should not have to choose between being fed and being safe. Nor should she have to wait until she can support herself before her family acknowledges that what is happening to her is wrong. We also need to reconsider the familiar instruction to “stay for the children”. What are the children experiencing while she stays? What are they learning about love, anger and power? Are they sleeping peacefully, or listening through the wall? Are they free to make ordinary mistakes, or already studying a parent’s mood before they speak? Esi’s daughter wanted to buy her mother a house so nobody could threaten to throw her out. A child had begun planning how to protect an adult. That should concern us far more than whether the family still appeared together in photographs. And abuse does not always leave a bruise. It can involve threats, humiliation, forced sex, isolation or control over money. It can mean needing permission to visit your own family, having every purchase interrogated, or being reminded that you have nothing and nobody without your spouse. When a woman finally speaks, she may be telling us only a small part of what she has endured. Our first response matters. “Are you safe?” “Do you need somewhere to stay?” “What can we do to help?” These questions give her room to speak. They do not demand that she explain why she stayed, why she did not report sooner or why she still has complicated feelings about the man who hurt her. For parents especially, a daughter must know that marriage has not closed the door behind her. She should be able to come home without first proving that she was a perfect wife. Esi still had difficult days ahead. There were expenses, decisions and moments when she doubted herself. Leaving did not make her life suddenly easy. But in her sister’s kitchen, her daughter spilled milk and was handed a cloth. That ordinary moment showed Esi how much fear had entered their everyday lives. The next time a woman tells us her husband has beaten her, let us resist the urge to investigate her tone, her cooking or her obedience. Let us hear what she has said. For parents especially, a daughter must know that marriage has not closed the door behind her. She should be able to come home without first proving that she was a perfect wife. The next time a woman tells us her husband has beaten her, let us hear what she has said. Before we ask what she did, let us ask whether she is safe. About the author Edith Agbeli is the Channel Manager of Joy Prime television.

items.title: Madonna University: ‘Give us second chance’ — Expelled nursing student pleads over TikTok challenge
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab A 500-level nursing student expelled by Madonna University, Rivers State, over a viral TikTok challenge has appealed to the institution to give her and other affected students a second chance, saying she is struggling with how to explain the development to her mother after years of study. The student, who is one of the students sanctioned by the university over a video of nursing students dancing within the institution’s teaching hospital, made the emotional appeal in a video that has now gone viral. “How do I explain to my mother? I’m one of the dozen students that was expelled. After all these years, how do I explain to my mother?” she said. The video was part of the “Gen Z nurses” social media trend and showed the students dancing in different parts of the hospital environment, including a waiting area, staircase and bus. The clip, reportedly captioned, “No fall sick o, na Gen Z full hospital now,” was uploaded in August before gaining wider attention after it was circulated by social media blogs. A 15-second version of the video on X on September 1 reportedly attracted more than 1.7 million views, while the original TikTok account was later made private. Madonna University confirmed that the video was recorded within its teaching hospital and subsequently took disciplinary action against the students involved. While some Nigerians have defended the university’s decision, arguing that students preparing to become nurses should understand the professional standards expected of them and the sensitivity of filming entertainment content in a hospital, others have called for leniency. The National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, has joined calls for clemency. NANS President, Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, acknowledged that the students’ conduct was inappropriate and contrary to the standards expected of nursing students. However, he appealed to Madonna University to reconsider the sanctions, arguing that the punishment could have a lasting effect on the students’ education and future careers. “Expulsion is, by far, a grave punishment. Beyond the immediate academic consequences, it can fundamentally alter the course of a young person’s life,” Afeez said. NANS subsequently urged the university to replace the expulsion with a stern warning, saying the students had invested years, resources and hopes in pursuing careers in nursing. The association said, “We appeal to the compassion and clemency of the Management of Madonna University to please save their future and give them a second chance.” Her plea comes as NANS, NUNSA and other stakeholders continue to call on Madonna University to reconsider the sanctions and give the affected students another opportunity. The post Madonna University: ‘Give us second chance’ — Expelled nursing student pleads over TikTok challenge appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tandjouaré/Education : Une convention de partenariat signée pour le maintien des enfants à l’école
items.description: Tandjouaré, 7 oct. (ATOP) – Des conventions-cadres de partenariat ont été signées, le mardi 6 octobre à Nano, entre la commune Tandjouaré 2 et l’ONG Action éducation, pour le maintien durable des enfants à l’école. L’initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet « Amélioration de l’accès et du maintien à l’école pour les enfants du Bénin et du Togo : Toutes et tous à l’école ». Elle vise à améliorer l’accès des enfants à l’éducation, à favoriser leur assiduité et leur maintien durable à l’école tout en renforçant la gouvernance scolaire locale et la collaboration des acteurs du secteur éducatif. La cérémonie a été marquée par la signature, d’une part, de l’accord entre Aide éducation et la commune, et d’autre part, d’un pacte communal avec l’Inspection d’enseignement préscolaire et primaire (IEPP), l’action sociale et le Comité de gestion des écoles primaires (COGEP). Les parties du pacte communal Le maire Kanye Djangré a indiqué que la réussite de ce projet reposera principalement sur la mobilisation des communautés locales, appelées à jouer un rôle central dans la sensibilisation des populations sur l’importance de la scolarisation. Il a relevé que plusieurs enfants en âge de scolarisation restent encore à la maison tandis que d’autres abandonnent leur parcours dès le primaire. Selon lui, le projet entend contribuer à récupérer ces enfants et à assurer leur maintien à l’école. Le chargé du projet, Mindeguelabe Koumbogle a indiqué que la formalisation de ce partenariat traduit la responsabilité partagée de faire de l’éducation une volonté partagée. « L’objectif est de traduire cet engagement par des actions concrètes, en réponses aux défis rencontrés en matière d’accès, d’assiduité et de maintien des enfants à l’école », a-t-il relevé. Le projet réalisé avec l’appui financier de l’Agence française de développement (AFD) court de 2026 à 2030. Il concerne les communes Cinkassé 2, Kpendjal-ouest 1, Kpendjal 2, Oti-sud 1 et Tandjouaré 2. ATOP/SYI/JK/DHK

items.title: Sudan war: Four women killed in drone strikes on Ed Damazin, Blue Nile
items.description: Four women have died and civilian sites, including a mosque and a technical college, were hit in drone strikes on Ed Damazin, capital of Sudan’s Blue Nile state, according to multiple sources. The home of the state finance minister was also hit. The attack on El Hijra neighbourhood damaged a mosque and killed four women: Nahed El Jundi Yassin, Hanaa El Jundi Yassin, Masajid Jaber Idris, and Himaya El Nour. Fighting has intensified in Blue Nile between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement. The bodies of the victims prepared for burial (Photo: RD) Finance minister’s home hit The Blue Nile Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning condemned the attack on the home of Finance Minister Molana Abbas Kara, which was struck by several missiles. Kara said on his official Facebook page that the RSF targeted his home with four missiles fired by a strategic drone, describing the incident as a failed assassination attempt. The home of the finance minister in the Blue Nile region was damaged in the attack (Photo: RD) Technical college damaged The administration of Ed Damazin Technical College condemned the attack on its campus by two drones, saying several lecture halls, administrative offices, laboratories, and other infrastructure were damaged or destroyed. It said attacks on educational institutions violate students’ and staff members’ right to a safe and stable learning environment and damage civilian infrastructure serving the wider community. Civilian protection urged Fawateh El Nour El Bashir, governor of Ed Damazin locality, condemned the attacks on residential neighbourhoods and civilian sites, which killed several people and injured others. The Blue Nile Civil Society Initiative also condemned the killing of the four women in El Hijra, attributing the strikes to the RSF and its allied Sudan People’s Liberation Movement. It also condemned the attack on the finance minister’s home in El Matar neighbourhood. The initiative’s secretary-general, Ali Hajo, told Radio Dabanga that four people were killed – two from the same family and two neighbours. He said the finance minister’s home was also targeted without causing human casualties, along with a mosque and other civilian sites. The Emergency Lawyers Group condemned the drone attacks in a statement seen by Radio Dabanga, warning against continued attacks on civilian sites. It said deliberately targeting civilians or civilian sites constitutes a serious violation of international humanitarian law, and called for the attacks to stop and those responsible to be held accountable. The group urged all parties to respect international humanitarian law and protect civilians and civilian sites. The Al Jazira Human Rights Observatory said the attacks had caused widespread fear and panic among residents. It expressed concern over attacks on populated areas and rising civilian casualties, noting that Ed Damazin shelters thousands of displaced people who have fled fighting elsewhere in the region. The observatory urged the parties to the conflict not to turn cities into arenas for fighting and military operations. items.title: CDF Munir reaffirms Pakistan’s commitment to international peace in meeting with UN chief
items.description: Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Wednesday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to international peace in a meeting with United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres, the military’s media affairs wing said. The UN secretary general is currently in Islamabad on a two-day official visit . In a statement on Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said Guterres called on CDF Munir at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi. “During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment and the UN’s role in promoting international peace and security were discussed,” it said. “The two sides exchanged views on regional stability, the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, India’s abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty and terrorism emanating from Afghanistan,” it added. During the meeting, CDF Munir also reaffirmed “Pakistan’s commitment to international peace and highlighted its contributions to UN peacekeeping missions”. He also lauded the UN’s role in “advancing peace, stability and humanitarian cooperation”. According to ISPR, the UN secretary general paid tribute to the sacrifices and contributions of Pakistan and its armed forces in the war against terror and in UN peacekeeping missions. “He also acknowledged Pakistan’s continued commitment to international peace and security,” ISPR said, adding that Guterres specifically appreciated “Pakistan’s efforts towards the peaceful resolution of regional conflicts”. On the first day of his trip, the UN secretary general held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. During the meeting, Guterres appreciated Pakistan’s “longstanding contribution to the UN, as well as its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation”. He also addressed a joint stakeout with Dar, during which he lauded Pakistan’s “pivotal role” in mediating between the United States and Iran as he called on the parties to end the conflict and return to diplomacy. President Asif Ali Zardari also conferred the Nishan-i-Imtiaz on Guterres in recognition of his “distinguished international service, leadership of the UN and contribution to global peace and development”. The two also held a separate meeting, where Zardari appreciated Guterres’ principled leadership, his efforts for international peace, dialogue, diplomacy and peaceful settlement of disputes, as well as his constructive engagement with Pakistan and attention to the concerns of developing countries.

items.title: “Wontumi doesn’t like where he is”– Palgrave Boakye
items.description: Spokesperson for incarcerated former Ashanti Regional New Patriotic Party (NPP) Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, says the latter is not happy with where he is. According to him, contrary to speculation by some people, Wontumi is currently serving his sentence at the Nsawam Prison. “People still don’t believe Chairman Wontumi is in prison, but the truth is he is there and not happy with where he is,” he said. Speaking on Adom FM’s Dwaso Nsem , Dr. Boakye Danquah said Wontumi was taken to prison immediately after all legal processes were completed on the day he was sentenced. “On the day he was sentenced, he went straight to Nsawam prison after all the processes were completed,” she said. He explained that he had learnt that prisoners are usually given about a week to put their affairs in order before beginning their sentences. “However, Wontumi had no grace period, and very soon, he would have served three months in prison,” he said while expressing concern about his continued detention. “What sent Wontumi to Nsawam was no case,” he said, insisting that his lawyers had filed an appeal against the sentence. “We have filed an appeal, and by next week, we will go to court,” he added. Dr. Boakye further noted that he was unhappy about an incident that occurred during the legal vacation. “During the legal vacation, there was a Zoom hearing, and the judge heard nine cases. Wontumi was the 10th person, but just when it got to his turn, the judge said he was sick and closed,” she said. Palgrave said she was saddened by Wontumi’s situation and expressed hope that the ongoing legal process would provide an opportunity for the matter to be reviewed. “I am really sad all this is happening,” she said. His comments follow President John Dramani Mahama’s recent decision to grant presidential pardons to some convicts. President Mahama announced the clemency as part of a special exercise covering 863 convicted persons nationwide. The announcement has drawn attention to several high-profile figures who may have been considered, among them Wontumi, whose case is still before the courts.

items.title: Kemi Seba: la justice sud-africaine ouvre la voie à son extradition vers le Bénin
items.description: Nouveau revers judiciaire pour Kemi Seba en Afrique du Sud. La justice de Pretoria a rejeté, le mardi 6 octobre 2026, sa demande d’immunité diplomatique, malgré son passeport diplomatique nigérien, ouvrant ainsi la voie à l’examen de la demande d’extradition formulée par le Bénin. L’audience sur le fond est prévue le 20 novembre 2026. La justice sud-africaine a rejeté, mardi 6 octobre 2026, la demande d’immunité diplomatique introduite par Kemi Seba, de son vrai nom Stellio Gilles Robert Capo Chichi. La décision permet désormais à la procédure d’extradition engagée par le Bénin de poursuivre son cours. Lors de l’audience tenue à Pretoria, les juges ont estimé que l’activiste ne pouvait pas se prévaloir d’un statut diplomatique. Kemi Seba dispose pourtant d’un passeport diplomatique délivré par le Niger et avait été nommé conseiller spécial par les autorités nigériennes. La justice sud-africaine n’a toutefois pas reconnu cette qualité, notamment au regard de sa nationalité béninoise. L’extradition en ligne de mire L’audience consacrée au fond de la demande d’extradition formulée par le Bénin a été fixée au 20 novembre 2026. La décision rendue le 6 octobre ne tranche donc pas encore la question de son éventuel retour au Bénin. Kemi Seba avait été arrêté en avril 2026 en Afrique du Sud, en compagnie de son fils et d’un facilitateur, alors qu’il s’apprêtait, selon les éléments de la procédure, à franchir illégalement la frontière en direction du Zimbabwe. Au Bénin, les autorités et la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et du terrorisme (Criet) le poursuivent notamment pour des faits qualifiés d’«apologie de crime contre l’État» et d’«incitation à la haine et à la violence», en lien avec son soutien exprimé par vidéo à une tentative de coup d’État survenue en décembre 2025. La procédure évoque également des soupçons de blanchiment de capitaux et de financement du terrorisme. La justice sud-africaine devra donc désormais se pencher sur le fond de la demande d’extradition. Pour Kemi Seba, la prochaine échéance judiciaire est fixée au 20 novembre, date à laquelle pourrait se jouer une nouvelle étape déterminante de cette procédure. En attendant, son éventuel retour au Bénin reste suspendu à l’issue de la procédure d’extradition engagée devant les juridictions sud-africaines. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Kemi Seba: la justice sud-africaine ouvre la voie à son extradition vers le Bénin est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

(ATOP) – Le conseil régional des Plateaux a ouvert, le mardi 6 octobre à Atakpamé, les travaux de sa quatrième session ordinaire, consacrés à l’état d’avancement des chantiers d’infrastructure dans les différentes préfectures de la région. Pendant quatre jours, les assises permettront aux élus régionaux d’évaluer, et de planifier les politiques publiques locales en faveur des populations. Elles constituent une étape déterminante dans l’agenda institutionnel de la région, offrant l’opportunité aux conseillers d’examiner les affaires inscrites à l’ordre du jour et d’adopter des résolutions pour assurer une gouvernance efficace. Au cœur des délibérations, figurent l’état d’avancement des chantiers d’infrastructure sanitaire au sein des principaux lycées des préfectures de la région. Il s’agira ainsi de dresser le bilan des réalisations, d’identifier les axes d’amélioration et d’établir une feuille de route prospective. L’ensemble de ces démarches s’insère dans une dynamique de consolidation de la décentralisation et de promotion d’un développement territorial équilibré. Le président de l’institution, Komlan Gnatcho a exhorté l’ensemble des acteurs régionaux à assurer un suivi rigoureux des opérations en cours. « Initiés au cours de l’année 2025, ces projets structurants feront l’objet d’un état des lieux détaillé afin de mesurer l’avancement physique des travaux dans chaque préfecture », a-t-il affirmé. Le gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, Gal de brigade Dadja Manganawé a convié les participants à s’investir pleinement dans les débats dans un esprit de concertation. Il a exprimé le vœu que les travaux débouchent sur des orientations stratégiques pertinentes et des décisions de nature à raffermir la gouvernance régionale et à accélérer le développement socio-économique au service du bien commun. items.title: Troops ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​​⁠⁠‌‌​⁠‌​repel ISWAP assault in Borno, kill over 20 terrorists
items.description: Troops of Operation Hadin Kai have repelled a coordinated multi-directional assault by ISWAP terrorists in Kukawa, Borno, reportedly neutralising more than 25 terrorists. The troops also recovered six AK-47 rifles and other arms and ammunition during the counter-offensive, according to a statement issued on Tuesday by Capt. Mohammed Goni, Acting Military Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force, North East. Goni said the terrorists attacked troops of 101 Special Forces Battalion from four directions but were met with stiff resistance. He said the troops, supported by the Air Component, responded with superior firepower and coordinated tactical manoeuvres, forcing the terrorists to flee in disarray. “Preliminary assessment indicates that over 25 terrorists were neutralised, with 14 bodies recovered so far,” he said. He said further exploitation of the area was ongoing to recover additional weapons, track fleeing terrorists and prevent them from regrouping. Goni said some soldiers were also killed during the encounter, describing them as gallant personnel who paid the supreme sacrifice in defence of the nation. He said the Nigerian Army had extended condolences to the families of the fallen soldiers and reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining pressure on terrorist groups. According to him, the successful repulsion of the assault demonstrated the combat readiness and resilience of troops in the North-East Theatre. He added that the operation also underscored the effectiveness of air-ground coordination and joint operations in disrupting terrorist activities. Goni said troops would continue aggressive patrols, intelligence-led operations and coordinated offensive actions with other security agencies to dismantle terrorist networks and protect communities. (NAN) The post Troops ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​​⁠⁠‌‌​⁠‌​repel ISWAP assault in Borno, kill over 20 terrorists appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PMDC reschedules NRE Step-1 for foreign medical graduates to Nov 8
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) has rescheduled the first step of the National Registration Examination (NRE) from Oct 11 to Nov 8. NRE is a mandatory requirement under an Act of Parliament, aimed at ensuring transparency, standardisation, and quality in medical and dental education and professional practice in Pakistan. In a notification dated Oct 5, the PMDC cited “unavoidable circumstances” for the move and said Step-1 of the NRE exam will now be held on Nov 8 (Sunday). A senior PMDC official told Dawn on Wednesday that the decision was made due to the prevailing political situation and possible road closures. The rescheduling comes after the PTI on Oct 4 launched a long march from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa towards Islamabad, despite warnings from the federal government against such a move. Authorities in Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory had intensified security arrangements to maintain law and order ahead of the PTI’s planned march. The march began from Lakki Marwat, reached the outskirts of Peshawar last night and plans to move towards Khairabad — which borders Punjab — by Oct 8, where the KP chief minister will announce the next plan of action. The National University of Medical Sciences in Rawalpindi is entrusted with conducting NRE to “ensure credibility, integrity, and transparency,” according to the PMDC . The exam is conducted in two steps at least twice a year in accordance with the approved NRE standards, structure, and syllabus, and as per a curriculum on par with the medicine and dentistry degrees in Pakistan. Foreign medical graduates who have earned degrees in medicine or dentistry in languages other than English have to clear two steps or the NRE exam in order to start house job and get a licence to practice in Pakistan.
