items.title: The Labadi shoreline demolitions: Who owns the beach?
items.description: At dawn of 2nd October 2026, there was a heavy deployment of excavators rudely awakening slumbering squatters, tearing down walls, kiosks, bars, and concrete extensions along the stretch of coast that hosts Labadi Pleasure Beach Resort and La Palm Royal Beach Hotel. For business owners, small vendors and tourists, it looked like destruction of investment, livelihood and leisure opportunity. For the adjoining SSNIT-owned resorts, it was years of trespassing on their littoral rights, grave nuisance, and obstruction of the visual amenity of the oceanfront. For the state, it was enforcement of growing flagrant encroachment and code violations and the need for a reset of law and order. It, however, raises a fundamental question that Ghana has avoided for decades: Who owns the shoreline? To get to the grind, four manifesting factors have necessitated the demolitions; The Law: The Foreshore squarely belongs to the State. Under Ghanaian law, the beach is not private property. For some entitled reasons, some traditional authorities erroneously assume that their land ownership extends to the shorelines. This has been reinforced by the lack of education and the general laxity on the enforcement of existing planning and zoning regulations. The Land Act, 2020 (Act 1036), the Constitution, and long-standing common law are clear: The foreshore — that is, the land between the high-water mark and low-water mark – and the land 50 to 100 meters inland from it, is public land vested in the President on behalf of the people. No individual, stool, family, or hotel can own it. What private persons own is the adjoining dry land. As it stands, Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Beach Resort hold leases for their parcels. The beach itself is held on permissive use. It remains a public amenity. Unfortunately, in the last 15 years, that permissive use turned into spontaneous accretion of permanent construction with some level of connivance of traditional authorities in the area. Concrete walls, permanent restaurants, nightclubs, swimming pools, and rental apartments were erected directly on the active beach, well within the high-water zone. Obviously, most had no permit from the Ghana Tourism Authority, no coastal development permit from the Land Use and Spatial Planning Authority (LUSPA), no Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) permit, and no building permits. Public Safety concerns arising from ocean erosion. The Greater Accra coastline has receded to a cumulative distance of 30meters since 2005, averaging between 2 to 4 meters per year. The unregulated physical structures disrupt littoral drift i.e., the natural movement of sand that forms an embankment and protects the beach from further erosion. The Enforcement of The New Coastal Buffer policy. In 2022, Cabinet approved a National Coastal Development Buffer 50 meters from the high-water mark for new development, and 100 meters in high-risk areas like Labadi, Ada and Elmina. Permanent structures are therefore not permitted inside this buffer without Cabinet approval. MMDAs within these designated coastal areas are mandated to enforce that buffer. The Labadi demolitions are the first high-profile application in Accra, following similar exercises in the Sakumono Ramsar site. The Rights of Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Beach Resort: This is where the current contention appears to lie. Adjoining landowners have two distinct rights in law: Right of Access: Littoral landowners have a common law right of access to and from the sea over the foreshore. They cannot be landlocked. They must have access to the beach by their littoral rights. They, however, don’t have automatic or natural rights to unobstructed views unless it was expressly granted in the title or deed. For instance, the littoral rights holder cannot prevent the construction of a sea defense wall under the State’s coastal protection program. However, there is a right to property enjoyment without nuisance. If the state or a neighbor creates a structure that completely obstructs visual access, impedes sewage, or creates noise and nuisance that undermine the value of a beachfront hotel, that can become a basis for compensation or an injunction under the law of nuisance under Article 20 of the Constitution. It is anticipated that following the demolition, clearing of debris and proper remediation actions would be taken to restore the shoreline as a managed public beach with the needed amenities like restrooms and lifeguards to enhance its healthy and safe public use. Arc. Frank Eshun 4/10/2026 Frank Eshun, a trained architect and a construction management professional, is the founder and President of Plannerx LLC, a Greater Charlotte-based licensed builder with operations in both North and South Carolina.

items.title: Marriage can be dissolved on a woman's initiative on grounds of shiqaq even if cruelty is not proven: SC
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that a marriage could be dissolved on grounds of shiqaq (marital discord) under a residuary provision of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 even when cruelty was not proven. The residuary provision of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 2(ix), explains the grounds on which a woman can obtain a decree for the dissolution of her marriage. In its judgement, the SC stated: “A marriage may be dissolved by a court, but neither spouse should be judicially deprived of a lawful right, nor judicially burdened with a stigma, without the foundation of law and evidence.” The judgement was issued by a five-member bench, headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhter Afghan, Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, Ishtiaq Ibrahim and Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb. The judges had taken up two connected petitions, filed by Zainab Bibi and Imran Naz Begum, against separate orders of the Peshawar High Court (PHC). Both cases arose from family suits where wives sought dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty and claimed maintenance, dower and dowry articles. The family court found cruelty unproven in both cases, but dissolved both marriages through khula — a woman’s right to seek release from a marriage. The family courts also directed the two women to return their dower, while the appellate court and the PHC largely upheld these decrees. The two women raised two principal grievances before the SC: first, that their marriages could not lawfully be dissolved through khula because they neither sought nor consented to it, as their cases were founded on cruelty; and second, their financial claims should have been allowed in full. The SC’s 15-page judgement on their please, authored by Justice Waheed, drew a distinction between khula and shiqaq and explained that khula proceeded from a wife’s voluntary election to obtain release from the marriage and ordinarily carried financial consequences. Shiqaq , by contrast, arose from an objectively established condition of serious matrimonial breach and did not depended on a wife’s surrender of dower or any benefit as consideration for her release, the judgement stated. The SC held that family courts committed an error in converting the petitioners’ claims for the dissolution of their marriages on the ground of cruelty into decrees of khula without obtaining their clear and voluntary consent or election. Those decrees, to the extent that they rested upon khula , could not be sustained, the judgement said, though the SC did not set aside the dissolution altogether. “The matrimonial relationships have undergone a serious and continuing rupture; reconciliation has failed; the evidence does not establish the statutory ground of cruelty; and the record, taken as a whole, establishes a condition of ‘ shiqaq ’ of the kind contemplated by verse 35 of Surah An-Nisa of the Holy Quran and recognised under Muslim law, thereby bringing the cases within the residuary provision contained in section 2(ix) of the Act of 1939,” the SC explained. The dissolution could therefore lawfully be sustained, but upon a juridical basis different from that adopted by the family courts, the SC judgement said, adding that marriages of the petitioners were liable to dissolution on the ground of shiqaq falling within section 2(ix) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, and not on the basis of khula . However, the directions requiring the petitioners to return, surrender or waive their dower merely as a consequence of khula should consequently stood set aside, the SC ruled. Their entitlement to dower would be determined in accordance with the Act of 1939, it declared. The SC observed that the Quranic emphasis upon reconciliation in cases of shiqaq was meaningful precisely because it contemplated the possibility that reconciliation may fail. “The law should neither rush towards separation nor prolong a matrimonial relationship which has ceased to serve its lawful purposes,” the judgement held. Where reconciliation had failed, and the relationship had reached the condition of shiqaq , the judicial task was to bring the matter to a lawful conclusion without unnecessary attribution of blame or deprivation of rights, the judgement explained. The SC emphasised that courts must distinguish between an unhappy marriage and one in a state of shiqaq . “Mere incompatibility, occasional disagreement, anger, short separation or the existence of matrimonial litigation cannot, by themselves, satisfy the test. The court must be satisfied that the breach is genuine, serious and continuing; that the matrimonial relationship has ceased to function in accordance with its essential purposes; and that reconciliation has failed despite meaningful judicial effort,” the judgement emphasised. The wife should not be compelled to surrender dower through an involuntary conversion of her statutory claim into khula , it said, adding that the husband should also not be judicially characterised as cruel or guilty of matrimonial misconduct without the evidentiary foundation required by law. “Allegations of cruelty, ill-treatment, neglect and misconduct frequently arise in an emotionally charged environment. The courtroom should not become an institution through which matrimonial discord is converted into a permanent injury to the reputation and dignity of either spouse,” it explained. The judgement further stated: “The law must determine rights; it need not aggravate human conflict. Where the evidence does not establish a particular matrimonial wrong to the standard required by law, the courts should refrain from declaring it proved. Conversely, where the evidence establishes that the matrimonial relationship itself has descended into a state of serious and continuing rupture, the absence of proof of a particular matrimonial wrong does not necessarily require parties to remain bound to one another indefinitely.” The judgement explained that shiqaq was not established by every quarrel, disagreement, incompatibility or temporary estrangement in a marriage. “It requires a genuine and continuing rupture of such character that the essential purposes of marriage cannot realistically be fulfilled, coupled with failure of reasonable efforts at reconciliation.”

items.title: Unemployment has dropped to 5% under Tinubu — Aremu
items.description: …as FG clears N758bn pension arrears By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – THE Director General, Michael Imoudu National Institute for Labour Studies, MINILS, Comrade Issa Aremu, Tuesday, asserted that the National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, unemployment figure is stable at five per cent, while the Federal Government has paid N758 billion in inherited pension liabilities, reflecting improving economic activity in both the public and private sectors. Aremu stated this during an interview on Arise TV Morning Show, where he addressed the administration’s labour and pension record. According to the labour leader, the NBS, applying the International Labour Organisation’s methodology, now puts the official unemployment rate at about five per cent, a marked improvement from the double-digit figures previously recorded. He said: “Today unemployment is about 5% officially. And that’s quite remarkable. You discover that unemployment dropped compared to what it used to be in double digits, which means there’s an increasing level of activity and employment, both in public and private sectors.” He also pointed to the opening up of the downstream sector, with modular refineries coming on stream and more people being engaged. He noted that the manufacturing sector had similarly reported upbeat prospects for job creation, though he stressed that sustainable industrialisation requires addressing the energy crisis, saying, “You can’t have sustainable industrialisation without electrification.” He further highlighted that many industries are now engaging in backward integration, sourcing raw materials locally due to the exchange rate, which is creating jobs at that level. The key to sustainable jobs, he argued, is that it “has to be deliberate” and led by states with appropriate industrial policies, welcoming the “Nigerian First” policy as it begins to gain traction. On the pension front, he (Aremu) commended the Federal Government’s N758 billion intervention bond, which has cleared inherited pension liabilities dating back to 2007. The payment reached 957,045 beneficiaries across Nigeria. The labour leader, who also serves as a member of the presidential campaign council, has said that labour issues around secured employment, living wages and pension payments will shape the next election. He tasked all leading candidates to present their scorecard with respect to decent and secured jobs, not promissory notes, adding that President Tinubu has commendably carried out reforms with job retention and expansion in the public sector, unlike mass retrenchment and downsizing that characterised previous reforms. He called for “job and wage-led economic recovery” adding that organised labour must in line with the tradition of unions, must engage the government for a negotiated new minimum wage. He commended the Tinubu administration for initiating two minimum wage reviews in three years. The post Unemployment has dropped to 5% under Tinubu — Aremu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 4è session ordinaire 2026 du Conseil régional des Savanes : Les acteurs planchent sur les priorités devant guider l’action de l’institution
items.description: Dapaong, 7 oct. (ATOP) – Le conseil régional des Savanes a ouvert, le mardi 6 octobre à Dapaong, les travaux de sa quatrième session ordinaire de l’année 2026, en présence du président, Banlepo Nabaguedjoa. La session est consacrée à l’examen des priorités devant guider l’action de l’institution régionale. Les travaux porteront notamment sur la présentation du Fonds d’appui aux collectivités territoriales (FACT), le débat d’orientation budgétaire, le point d’exécution des projets prévus en 2025 et 2026, ainsi que l’examen et le vote du budget primitif, exercice 2027. Le président du conseil régional a invité les conseillers régionaux à mener les travaux dans un esprit constructif, avec pour priorité l’intérêt général et le développement de la région des Savanes. M. Nabaguedjoa a relevé les avancées enregistrées par l’institution depuis le début de l’année, notamment dans la réalisation d’infrastructures sociales. Il a cité le lancement des travaux de construction de quatre maternités, la remise de sites pour la construction de dix bâtiments scolaires et l’acquisition de 1 200 bancs destinés aux établissements scolaires bénéficiaires. Le conseil régional a également remis 80 kits scolaires aux meilleurs élèves de la région, ainsi que des vivres et des non-vivres au centre de santé mentale et à l’hôpital mère-enfant Yendoubé de Tantigou. Pour le président, ces actions traduisent la volonté de l’institution de rendre visible les effets de la décentralisation auprès des populations. Il a, par ailleurs, annoncé la tenue, du 21 au 27 décembre prochain à Dapaong, de la première édition de la Foire agro-pastorale, artisanale et commerciale des Savanes. « Cette manifestation vise à promouvoir les productions locales et à offrir aux acteurs économiques un cadre de promotion et de recherche de débouchés », a-t-il déclaré. Le gouverneur de la région des Savanes, Atcha-Dédji Affoh a salué la collaboration et la complémentarité qui existent entre le conseil régional et les services de l’État. Il a exhorté les acteurs à mener des débats fructueux devant aboutir à des conclusions permettant de renforcer l’efficacité de l’action du conseil régional et de contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. ATOP/TK/JK/SED

items.title: Cedi will continue to be stable – Deputy Finance Minister
items.description: The Deputy Finance Minister, Thomas Nyarko Ampem, has assured that the cedi will remain stable, describing the stability of the local currency as a major relief for households seeking to finance their homes. His comments come as the cedi trades at about GH¢11.80 to the US dollar on the Bank of Ghana’s interbank market, based on the latest published rate. Speaking at the National Conference on Housing and Finance, he said a stable cedi would help families manage their housing costs without having to worry about fluctuations in the exchange rate. “Thankfully, under the competent leadership of His Excellency President Mahama and Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, the cedi has been stable and it will continue to be stable. That is a big relief,” he said. According to him, exchange rate stability is particularly important for households whose incomes are denominated in cedis, as currency fluctuations can affect their ability to meet financial obligations. “A family should not need to forecast the exchange rate to know whether it can keep its home,” he added. The Deputy Finance Minister also said the government would pursue measures to reduce the cost and risks associated with housing delivery. He noted that access to finance alone would not be enough to address Ghana’s housing affordability challenges, stressing the need for clear land ownership, realistic construction costs, reliable demand and workable infrastructure plans. He further identified predictable local approval processes and serviced land as important conditions for attracting investment into the housing sector.

items.title: Minority urges full probe into World Cup visa allegations after Ampofo Ankrah’s removal
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has welcomed President John Mahama’s decision to remove Yaw Ampofo Ankrah as Director-General of the National Sports Authority (NSA), but says his removal must be followed by a comprehensive investigation into alleged irregularities surrounding visa arrangements for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The Minority said its earlier call for Mr Ampofo Ankrah to step aside was based on concerns that the allegations required accountability and an independent investigation. Addressing the media on Wednesday, October 7, Ranking Member of Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, commended President Mahama for acting on the Minority’s demand. “We raised that call because we believed that, in the face of the serious questions surrounding the alleged World Cup visa arrangements, there was a need for accountability and for the investigation to proceed without the continued presence of the Director-General at the helm of affairs at the institution,” he said. Mr Assafuah, however, stressed that the removal of the NSA Director-General should not be treated as the end of the matter. He said documents and records available to the Minority suggested that the alleged irregularities involved a wider chain of institutional actors, requiring investigations beyond the former NSA Director-General. The Minority is calling for investigations into the roles of Sports and Recreation Minister Kofi Adams, the leadership of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA), officials of the National Sports Authority, officials within the Ministry of Sports and Recreation, and private entity TRIBE Culture Fest. The Minority wants the investigation to examine alleged visa-related irregularities and other concerns linked to Ghana’s preparations for the 2026 World Cup, including claims that unauthorised visa processing fees were charged to applicants. It has also raised concerns about the submission of individuals with questionable professional credentials to the United States and Canadian embassies as part of arrangements for the tournament. The Minority has previously alleged that more than US$600,000 was collected from individuals seeking assistance with visa and travel arrangements, with some applicants allegedly paying as much as US$8,000.

items.title: Zio/conseil régional Maritime : La 4e session ordinaire placée sous le signe de l’efficacité et de la redevabilité
items.description: Tsévié, 7 oct. (ATOP) – Le Conseil régional Maritime (CRM) a ouvert, le mardi 6 octobre à Tsévié, sa 4 ème session ordinaire de l’année 2026 placée sous le signe de l’efficacité et de la redevabilité. Cette dernière session de l’année 2026 va durer dix jours et sera échelonnée sur deux mois. Elle sera consacrée à la gouvernance, à l’évaluation des projets de développement et à la programmation budgétaire de la région Maritime. Au cours des travaux, les conseillers régionaux suivront un renforcement de capacités sur la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route 2025-2027 à travers les Plans de travail budgétaires annuels (PTBA). Ils évalueront l’état d’avancement des projets 2026 et adopteront des mesures d’amélioration concrète. D’autres sujets de ces assises porteront sur la restitution de la campagne de distribution des Moustiquaires imprégnées d’insecticide (MII) menée dans la région de Maritime. De plus, il est prévu l’examen de dossiers institutionnels majeurs, notamment l’adoption officielle du nouveau logo du CRM et les stratégies de mobilisation des ressources présentées par la commission des finances. Les conseillers régionaux plancheront sur le Débat d’orientation budgétaire (DOB), véritable boussole des choix économiques de la région. La session s’achèvera le 16 décembre prochain par l’examen du budget primitif 2027 et la présentation de la Cour des comptes. Le gouverneur de la région Maritime, Taïrou Bagbiègue a souligné que le Président du Conseil met au premier rang, la gouvernance locale avec ses deux niveaux de décentralisation que sont les communes et les régions. Pour le président du CRM, Edoh Komla, cette session est à la fois stratégique et fonctionnelle, car elle se situe non seulement au cœur de la feuille de route du Conseil régional Maritime, mais surtout dans la grande feuille de route gouvernementale 2026-2031. Pour le président Edoh Komla, cette quatrième session ordinaire est fondamentalement budgétaire parce qu’elle doit permettre à travers le débat d’orientation budgétaire, de consulter les citoyens, de prendre à cœur leurs préoccupations, en vue de se projeter à travers le budget primitif exercice 2027. ATOP/BBG/AR

items.title: Asiedu Nketiah backs greater church role in running mission schools
items.description: National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has backed calls for greater involvement of churches in the management of mission schools, arguing that stronger participation by the founding religious bodies could encourage further investment in education. He said churches and other religious organisations had historically played a major role in the development of education in Ghana and should have a meaningful role in the management of the institutions they established. Mr Asiedu Nketiah made the remarks at the centenary celebration of the Seventh-day Adventist (SDA) Church at Sekyedumase in the Ejura-Sekyedumase Municipality of the Ashanti Region. He was speaking at the launch of an initiative by the SDA Church to establish a College of Education at Sekyedumase as part of activities marking its 100th anniversary. The proposed college is expected to expand access to teacher education and create opportunities for young people in the area. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said the motivation for churches to establish and invest in schools was not limited to academic education, but also included the desire to raise children within the values and principles of their respective faiths. He argued that government financial support for mission schools should not necessarily mean that the religious bodies that established them should lose their role in shaping their identity and values. “The main driving force for religious bodies to invest in the building of schools is the need for their members to bring up their children in the core beliefs and discipline of their faith,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said the argument that churches should lose their role in teaching the basic tenets of their faith in mission schools because the State also invested public funds in them was flawed. He said parents whose children attended such schools were also taxpayers and, therefore, contributed to the public resources used to support the institutions. “The missions were the pioneers of education in the Gold Coast and continue to play a key role in the sector to date. The fact that most of the so-called Grade A schools are mission schools implies that there is something they are doing right which must be encouraged rather than diluted,” he said. He maintained that parents and students exercised a choice when applying to schools and that admission into a particular mission school should come with an understanding of its ethos and disciplinary requirements. “Parents and their wards are free to exercise their rights of choice at the point of application for admission. Once admitted to their choice of school, they have already committed to the disciplinary code of the school,” he said. His comments come amid an ongoing national debate over the management and religious identity of government-assisted mission schools. The Christian Council of Ghana and the Ghana Catholic Bishops’ Conference have argued that government assistance to mission schools should not be equated with state ownership or control, while also maintaining that students’ constitutional rights must be respected. A Memorandum of Understanding on religious tolerance and freedom in private and government-assisted mission schools was facilitated by the National Peace Council as part of efforts to provide a framework for managing religious diversity in such institutions. The debate has consequently centred on how to balance the religious character of mission-founded schools with constitutional guarantees of freedom of religion, equality and access to education.

items.title: Élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis : quel scénario selon les résultats ?
items.description: Le 3 novembre, les électeurs américains se rendront aux urnes pour les élections de « mi-mandat » ( midterms ). Sont en jeu les 435 sièges de la Chambre des représentants et 35 des 100 sièges du Sénat, ainsi que de nombreux mandats locaux. La très courte majorité républicaine à la Chambre et la majorité, un peu plus confortable, au Sénat sont toutes deux menacées. À en juger par les indicateurs disponibles, les démocrates semblent bien partis pour réaliser une bonne performance. Il n’est pas inhabituel que le parti du président sortant essuie un revers lors de ces élections, mais les sondages sont particulièrement défavorables aux républicains pour cette échéance de 2026. Le président lui-même affiche des niveaux de popularité historiquement faibles — les sondages récents situent son taux d’approbation autour de 38 % — et les perspectives de la plupart des candidats républicains au Congrès sont étroitement liées au sort politique de Trump. La campagne militaire de l’administration en Iran, impopulaire, ainsi que les questions liées au coût de la vie ont rendu les électeurs américains particulièrement mécontents ces derniers mois. Dans les sondages « génériques », les démocrates devancent les républicains de 8 points ou davantage, soit bien au-delà de la marge d’erreur. Plus révélateur encore, les républicains consacrent de plus en plus de ressources à défendre des sièges dans des territoires que Trump avait remportés largement en 2024. Dans des États comme le Texas, l’Iowa, l’Ohio et l’Alaska, où les républicains ont largement dominé ces dernières années, le parti du président est désormais sur la défensive. Les démocrates ont eux aussi leurs difficultés, et l’image du parti est loin d’être excellente auprès de nombreux électeurs, mais ils devraient néanmoins réaliser une bonne performance. Les chances des démocrates de reprendre la Chambre des représentants sont très bonnes. Il leur suffit de gagner trois sièges nets pour obtenir la majorité, et ils semblent bien placés pour y parvenir. Le Sénat est plus compliqué. Initialement, la carte électorale de cette année n’était pas particulièrement favorable à la minorité démocrate, mais, ces derniers mois, la dynamique semble s’être retournée contre plusieurs candidats républicains vulnérables. Certains pronostics donnent désormais un léger avantage aux démocrates, qui pourraient, tout juste, parvenir à remporter les quatre sièges nécessaires pour faire basculer le Sénat. Ce sera extrêmement serré. Si les démocrates parviennent à s’imposer dans les deux chambres, le changement sera probablement plus progressif que radical. Le chef de la minorité démocrate à la Chambre, Hakeem Jeffries, serait bien placé pour devenir président de la Chambre ( Speaker ). Jeffries est politiquement situé au centre-gauche et est étroitement lié à l’ establishment démocrate. Au Sénat, le chef de la minorité, Chuck Schumer, qui a déjà occupé le poste de chef de la majorité, convoite clairement cette fonction. Il rencontrera probablement une certaine opposition, mais il est le favori présumé. Schumer est lui aussi un pragmatique et un institutionnaliste. Ces deux dirigeants sont assez éloignés de certains des progressistes les plus en vue du parti, comme Bernie Sanders ou Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. Pour Donald Trump, en revanche, le retour de l’une ou des deux chambres du Congrès sous contrôle démocrate constituera presque certainement un casus belli . Avec une majorité démocrate au Congrès, les deux dernières années de la présidence Trump seront sans doute exceptionnellement houleuses et conflictuelles. Voici trois pronostics pour la période qui suivra les midterms : En cas de victoire démocrate, Donald Trump contribuera davantage encore à saper la confiance dans le système démocratique américain . Le président est certainement conscient des perspectives médiocres des républicains et semble avoir eu du mal à trouver un message susceptible d’améliorer leurs chances tout en prenant ses distances avec une éventuelle défaite électorale. Au lendemain d’une mauvaise élection pour les républicains, il est toutefois très probable que Trump et son administration mettent en cause la fiabilité du système électoral lui-même. Trump a attaqué à plusieurs reprises le vote par correspondance, affirmé que des non-citoyens, supposément favorables aux démocrates, votaient en grand nombre, et accusé de fraude toute une série de responsables électoraux locaux dans des circonscriptions favorables aux démocrates. Il a même été question de déployer des agents fédéraux, notamment du FBI et de l’ICE, dans les bureaux de vote à travers le pays. Si son parti perd, il faut s’attendre à des accusations virulentes de « vol » de l’élection de la part de Trump, avec les effets corrosifs que l’on peut imaginer sur la culture démocratique américaine lorsqu’un président des États-Unis formule de telles accusations. Les recours judiciaires infondés que les républicains pourraient engager contre les résultats électoraux n’auraient guère plus de chances d’aboutir que ceux de 2020, lorsque Trump avait déjà cherché à « stop the steal » après avoir perdu l’élection présidentielle. Mais le mal, lui, serait déjà fait. La paralysie gouvernementale sera inévitable. En cas de victoire démocrate, les chances de parvenir à un accord bipartisan sur les éléments fondamentaux de la gouvernance au cours des deux années qui resteront à Trump à la Maison-Blanche seraient pratiquement nulles. On peut notamment s’attendre à des affrontements persistants et perturbateurs autour du processus budgétaire. Des shutdowns de plusieurs semaines, voire de plusieurs mois, sont très probables. Contrairement à ses prédécesseurs, Trump semble avoir une grande tolérance pour le fait de mettre à l’arrêt une grande partie du gouvernement plutôt que de parvenir à un compromis négocié avec le Congrès, et il a déjà utilisé la menace d’un shutdown comme arme dans ses affrontements avec le Congrès. On peut espérer qu’il n’ira pas jusqu’à provoquer un défaut de paiement de la dette américaine, mais le président a démontré qu’il était à l’aise avec le recours au bras de fer autour du relèvement du plafond de la dette, avec des risques potentiellement considérables pour l’économie internationale si un différend avec le Congrès sur cette question restait sans solution. En cas de shutdown , Trump pourrait également recourir à des moyens juridiques contestables pour poursuivre certaines opérations gouvernementales qu’il juge prioritaires — la guerre en Iran ou les opérations de l’ICE contre les immigrés, par exemple. Le Congrès contre-attaquera. Les chances de voir Donald Trump faire une nouvelle fois l’objet d’une procédure de destitution sont élevées. Le Congrès pourrait invoquer plusieurs motifs, mais l’une des voies d’attaque qui présenterait certains avantages politiques pour les démocrates pourrait concerner les opérations militaires controversées menées par Trump en Iran. En vertu du War Powers Act , le président est légalement tenu d’informer le Congrès dans les 48 heures suivant le lancement d’opérations militaires et de solliciter une autorisation du Congrès dans un délai de 60 jours. Trump n’a fait ni l’un ni l’autre. La Chambre disposerait très certainement des voix nécessaires à une mise en accusation — l’équivalent, aux États-Unis, d’un acte d’accusation contre le président — et, si les démocrates contrôlent également la chambre haute, un procès se tiendrait au Sénat. Compte tenu de la majorité des deux tiers nécessaire pour condamner le président, une destitution effective paraît très improbable. À la Maison-Blanche comme au Congrès, cependant, une grande partie du travail quotidien risque de s’arrêter tandis que les deux branches du gouvernement se livreront une véritable guerre institutionnelle. Parallèlement, le Congrès mènera des auditions hostiles et pourrait même engager des procédures de destitution contre d’autres responsables de l’administration. En cas de victoire démocrate aux midterms , la fin de la présidence Trump risque donc d’être particulièrement difficile. Retrouvez régulièrement les éditos de Jeff Hawkins, ancien diplomate américain, chercheur associé à l’IRIS, pour ses Carnets d’un vétéran du State Department. L’article Élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis : quel scénario selon les résultats ? est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: La justicia rechaza de nuevo el desalojo de la Puerta del Sol porque no existe “inactividad” de la Delegación del Gobierno
items.description: El Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Madrid (TSJM) ha rechazado el desalojo por la fuerza de la acampada de la Puerta del Sol, instalada hace 11 días por la crisis de la vivienda en España . La Comunidad de Madrid presentó un recurso contencioso-administrativo en el que denunciaba la “ocupación ilegal de un espacio público” y aducía la “inactividad de la Delegación del Gobierno”, por lo que pedía la evacuación de forma inmediata. Dos días después, la Delegacion del Gobierno ha respondido con su oposición a la expulsión de los acampados y alega que esta medida puede ser “más perjudicial” que permitir el asentamiento. Para el TSJM esta inacción de la que habla el Gobierno regional no ha quedado demostrada y, por tanto, la medida cautelar ha sido desestimada. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tone : Des Journées portes ouvertes pour renforcer la confiance entre la police et les populations
items.description: Dapaong, 7 oct. (ATOP) – Les Journées portes ouvertes (JPO) de la Police nationale se tiennent du 6 au 8 octobre à Dapaong, à l’intention des populations de la région des Savanes. L’ouverture a été présidée par le gouverneur de la région des Savanes, Atcha-Dédji Affoh, en présence des autorités administratives, judiciaires et locales, des responsables des forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi que des représentants des populations. Ces journées visent à permettre au public de mieux connaître le fonctionnement et les missions de la police nationale. Elles constituent également une occasion de renforcer la confiance mutuelle entre l’institution policière et les populations. L’événement est marqué par des démonstrations, des expositions, des présentations des différents services et des échanges avec les personnels de la police nationale. Une opération foraine d’établissement de cartes nationales d’identité (CNI) est également organisée au profit des populations. Les officiels au lancement des JPO Le gouverneur de la région des Savanes a affirmé que ces journées constituent un cadre de rencontre, d’information et de sensibilisation permettant aux citoyens de mieux comprendre les missions, les responsabilités, les contraintes et les exigences liées au travail quotidien des policiers. Il a rappelé que la sécurité ne repose pas uniquement sur les opérations de contrôle, les interventions ou le maintien de l’ordre, mais également sur la proximité, l’écoute, la prévention, la sensibilisation et le dialogue permanent avec les citoyens. Le gouverneur a, par ailleurs, souligné l’importance de la collaboration entre les forces de sécurité et les communautés dans la région des Savanes. « Les populations constituent des partenaires essentiels de l’action sécuritaire, notamment parce qu’elles sont les premières à observer les changements dans leur environnement et à identifier certaines situations inhabituelles », a-t-il indiqué. Il a invité les jeunes de la région à profiter de ces journées pour découvrir les métiers de la Police nationale, estimant que ces rencontres pourraient également susciter des vocations. Le directeur du secteur de police nᵒ 5, le commissaire Sogan Koffi, a rappelé que la Police nationale est une institution au service de la population, chargée notamment de protéger les personnes et les biens, de maintenir l’ordre public, de prévenir la délinquance et de garantir la sécurité, dans le respect des lois et des libertés individuelles. Il a mis en avant les valeurs qui guident l’action des policiers, notamment l’intégrité, le professionnalisme, la disponibilité, le dépassement de soi et le dévouement au service de la nation. Pour le commissaire Sogan Koffi, ces journées constituent également une occasion de renforcer la confiance entre les forces de sécurité et la population, la sécurité demeurant une responsabilité partagée fondée sur la coopération, l’écoute et le respect mutuels. ATOP/TKA/JK/MD

items.title: Zio : La Police nationale en journées portes ouvertes à Tsévié
items.description: Tsévié, 7 oct. (ATOP) – Les journées portes ouvertes de la Police nationale ont débuté, le mardi 6 octobre à Tsévié, avec pour objectif de rapprocher les forces de sécurité des populations et de renforcer le dialogue et la confiance entre les deux parties. Organisées par la direction générale de la Police nationale, ces journées se poursuivent jusqu’au jeudi 8 octobre dans la cour du commissariat central de Tsévié, dans le secteur de police n°1. Les visiteurs peuvent découvrir l’organisation, les missions et les différents métiers de la Police nationale. Ils sont également informés sur les conditions de recrutement, les grades, les droits et devoirs des policiers, ainsi que les règles de discipline. Le programme comprend aussi des séances de sensibilisation sur la cybercriminalité, la sécurité routière, les stupéfiants, les violences, le viol, les braquages et le transport de fonds. Des quiz sont également prévus. Les populations peuvent par ailleurs bénéficier de certaines prestations administratives, notamment la légalisation de pièces et l’établissement accéléré de cartes nationales d’identité. Le gouverneur de la région Maritime, Taïrou Bagbiègue, a rappelé que la sécurité est essentielle à la stabilité, à la cohésion sociale et au développement économique. « Aucun progrès durable ne peut être envisagé dans un environnement marqué l’insécurité et l’instabilité », a-t-il a affirmé. Le gouverneur a invité les populations à participer aux différentes activités prévues. Le directeur de la première région de Police, le commissaire divisionnaire Kombaté Yendoula, a indiqué que cette initiative permettra aux populations de mieux connaître les missions de la Police nationale, son personnel et les valeurs qui guident son action, notamment l’intégrité, le professionnalisme, la disponibilité et le dévouement au service de la nation. ATOP/BBG/AO/BV

items.title: Nasarawa Assembly probes multiple taxation of businesses
items.description: …sets up ad hoc committee for investigation By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State House of Assembly has raised concerns over multiple taxation, saying the practice is imposing hardship on businesses and residents across the state. Speaker of the House, Dr Danladi Jatau, raised the concern while reading the House’s resolution on a Matter of Public Importance brought by Hon. Daniel Oga Ogazi during plenary on Tuesday in Lafia. Jatau said multiple taxation was negatively affecting businesses and the livelihoods of residents, urging relevant authorities to address the situation. He called on the state government to ensure full implementation of the State Revenue Harmonisation Law to eliminate multiple taxation. The Speaker also announced the constitution of an ad hoc committee to investigate revenue collection and determine the number of consultants collecting revenues in the state, as well as assess the implementation of the Revenue Harmonisation Law. The committee is chaired by Hon. Hudu A. Hudu, while other members are Hon. Daniel Ogazi, Hon. Solomon Yakubu Akwashiki, Hon. Jonah Ali Dizaho and Dr Hajara Danyaro Ibrahim. The Secretary is the Secretary of the House Committee on Finance and Appropriation, Mr Aluma Joseph. Jatau directed the committee to ascertain the state’s payees in the Mararaba axis of Karu Local Government Area and its environs, particularly whether businesses in border communities were paying revenues to Nasarawa State or other jurisdictions. He directed the committee to submit its report within two weeks. Earlier, Ogazi, who raised the matter, said businesses were being subjected to multiple taxes, adding that the situation was worsening the economic hardship faced by residents. “Business people are complaining of paying multiple taxes and this is causing hardship to our people. A proprietor of a private school complained of paying 23 multiple taxes,” he said. Ogazi said multiple taxation was discouraging business activities and compounding the hardship caused by prevailing economic conditions. He urged the House to direct the State Revenue Service to intensify efforts to address the issue. Contributing to the debate, lawmakers including Hon. Esson Mairiga, Hon. Hudu A. Hudu, Hon. Jacob Ajegena Kudu, Hon. Hajara Danyaro Ibrahim, Hon. Musa Abubakar Ibrahim, Rt. Hon. Abel Yakubu Bala, Hon. Larry Ven-Bawa and Rt. Hon. Mohammed Adamu Oyanki expressed support for the motion. They said the House would not allow businesses to collapse in the state as a result of multiple taxation. The lawmakers also said multiple taxation could discourage investment and worsen economic hardship, calling on the state and local governments to ensure full implementation of the Revenue Harmonisation Law passed by the House. The post Nasarawa Assembly probes multiple taxation of businesses appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le Nobel de chimie décerné à un duo franco-japonais
items.description: Le prix Nobel de chimie a été attribué, mercredi, au Français Henri Kagan et au Japonais Kenso Soai pour leurs recherches en catalyse asymétrique. « Leurs découvertes ont joué un rôle déterminant pour les chimistes qui conçoivent des réactions destinées à la fabrication de produits pharmaceutiques », a salué le comité Nobel dans un communiqué. Âgé de 95 ans, le professeur Kagan est actuellement professeur à l'université Paris-Saclay. « C'est le jour le plus incroyable de ma vie » , a réagi par téléphone le lauréat de 76 ans, Kenso Soai, professeur à l'université des sciences naturelles de Tokyo. La chimie est le troisième prix scientifique des Nobel, après la médecine et la physique, attribués lundi et mardi derniers. Cette année, les pronostics des experts pour les lauréats se partageaient entre des domaines très divers : thérapie génique, hormones du sommeil et monocouches auto-assemblées. Le prestigieux prix Nobel récompense ses lauréats par un diplôme, une médaille d'or et environ un million d'euros. La saison d'attribution se terminera le 12 octobre avec le prix d'économie. The post Le Nobel de chimie décerné à un duo franco-japonais appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Galamsey activities redirect Mankran Stream, destroy farms, and threaten flooding in Okroase
items.description: Residents of Okroase in the Ahafo Ano Southwest district of the Ashanti Region are living in fear over a possible flooding situation as illegal mining operations redirect the flow of the Mankran Stream. Already, the diverted milky sludge from the water body from the artisanal mining activities has destroyed several acres of rice farms and a commercial coconut and oil palm nursery, running into millions of cedis. Emmanuel Amponsah was visibly distraught over the destruction of his over 200,000 cedis worth of investment in oil palm and coconut seedling plantations. He nursed the seedlings for months, hoping to raise healthy planting materials for farmers and land reclamation projects. Footage captured days when the Mankran Stream, heavily laden with silt, overflowed its banks and flooded the nursery. After the water receded, the extent of destruction remains visible. The once-thriving nursery is now covered in mud and debris, with several coconut and oil palm seedlings completely damaged. “I regret coming here. I was at Mankranso, and they destroyed over 2,000 seedlings there. I came here only for this to happen again. It’s like a perennial problem,” he worriedly said. Just across from Amponsah’s nursery, another farmer is counting his losses. Nana Yaw and his wife cultivated their rice plantation at the beginning of the year, looking forward to a good harvest to support their household. But today, they watch, in discontent, their one-acre rice farm now submerged in milky sludge from the Mankran River. “This is very sad. No farmer would be happy seeing their farm in this bad state. I have made losses,” Nana Yaw said. His wife continued that: “It’s not as if the rice couldn’t grow bountifully. It did, but the water has destroyed everything. The illegal miners care less about us”. The cause of the devastation on the two farms sits only a few kilometers away – illegal mining. For months, miners have excavated land close to farmlands and residential areas, leaving behind heaps of excavated material. The farmers say the earthworks have altered the natural course of the stream, forcing water into adjoining farms. Effluent and heavy sediment from the mining areas have also accumulated in the waterway, choking culverts beneath a nearby bridge. Community folks made efforts to halt their operations, but the miners continue to dig deep into the earth’s crust, with the nearby communities bearing the brunt of the devastation. “I went there to sack them, but I was told they came back. Should our children and parents die before they stop?” a resident asked. The Mankran stream is traditionally one of Ghana’s oldest rivers, historically believed to be protected by a powerful river deity named Nana Mankran. For generations, the water body remained clear and pure, serving as the primary source for drinking, domestic chores, farming, and local fishing. But the same can’t be said now. It is now a pale shadow of the once crystal-clear water body. “We used to drink and swim in the stream. But we can’t do that now due to illegal mining,” Kontihene for the community said. Driving from Okroase through adjoining communities, including Kunsu and Mankranso, the signs of land degradation are difficult to miss. Large stretches of land along the Mankranso-Tepa Road have been excavated, leaving behind exposed earth and abandoned mining pits. Satellite imagery of the area also shows extensive muddy patches across what was previously green agricultural land. The communities have pushed for local government authorities to halt the operations and de-silt the waterway, but that seems to have fallen on deaf ears. “They promised to de-silt during the harmattan. We’ve informed the assemblyman several times,” the unit committee chairperson for the area said. But with the rainy season and the stream already struggling to contain its flow, residents say the danger remains. They fear a major downpour could send floodwaters into nearby homes and farms, causing even greater damage. “Whenever it floods, the water enters our home. We don’t want any disaster here,” the Kontihene indicated. Back on Amponsah’s farm, he grows the seedlings to support reclamation of degraded lands and for cash crop production. Amponsah usually cultivates 58 plant species, including citrus fruits and tree crops, but the incessant destruction of his nursery is compelling him to cut down to 6 plants for the new planting season. For now, farmers and residents say they need immediate intervention to restore the natural flow of the Mankran Stream, protect their farms, and prevent a possible flood disaster. Until that happens, the people of Okroase remain anxious each time the rains begin.

items.title: WiSTEM Ghana Camp assembles 320 girls to explore STEM education
items.description: Head of the Responsible Artificial Intelligence Lab (RAIL) at KNUST, Professor Jerry John Kponyo, has emphasized the need for deliberate and greater inclusion of women and girls in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education. Prof. Kponyo made these remarks at the 7th edition of the WiSTEM Ghana Camp, held under the theme “Give to Gain: Spark Her STEM Power”. He observed that although the country had made significant strides in girls’ inclusion in science and technology, more needed to be done to increase their participation. The WiSTEM Ghana Camp seeks to inspire and equip young girls with the knowledge, exposure and support needed to pursue careers in STEM. The camp, which assembled over 300 girls, aimed at developing the skills and confidence needed to pursue opportunities in science and technology. Prof. Kponyo noted that RAIL’s support for the programme is driven by the belief that no gender should be left behind in technological advancement, noting that there remains a gap in the participation of women in technology. He said the camp provides an opportunity to nurture the interest girls are already showing in STEM through practical experiences and support from parents, teachers, tertiary institutions and industry. “Primarily, is it important that the little initiative shown by these girls due to the interest in STEM which needs watered doing so involves hands-on-deck approach, parents and teachers have a role to played,” he said. Participants were exposed to hands-on activities at the Responsible AI Lab, where they could work on projects aimed at solving real-life problems employing science and technology. They engaged in practical sessions, laboratory activities and field trips designed to stimulate their interest in STEM. Prof. Kponyo also emphasized STEM investment extensions to young people in rural and underserved communities, noting that talented students in the hinterlands should also have the opportunity to realize their potential. According to him, the experience would help the girls appreciate that science goes beyond classroom theory and can be used to improve lives. “If we believe STEM is what will change the world, then we should make investments in the same. Irrespective of where people are, even people in the rural areas should benefit as far as STEM is concerned,” he added. Acting Pro Vice-Chancellor of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Professor Kwabena Biritwum Nyarko, touted the university’s support for the WiSTEM Ghana programme over the years. “WiSTEM is a programme to encourage and provide tools to young girls to pursue their dreams in STEM and for more sponsors to support the programme,” he noted. He stressed that investment in STEM education, research and innovation is essential if Ghana seeks to achieve its development aspirations. Professor Biritwum Nyarko further called on industry players and individuals to provide more funding, mentorship, industrial tours and internship opportunities to support the programme.

items.title: Russia launches heavy strikes at Ukraine, killing at least 20
items.description: Russia pounded Ukraine with waves of missiles and drones in one of its most “vile strikes” on Wednesday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, killing at ​least 20 people, including children, and damaging industrial facilities and energy infrastructure. Zelenskiy said the strike coincided with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s birthday. The heaviest death toll was in Pryluky in ‌the northern Chernihiv region, where a Russian missile obliterated a five-storey residential building. At least 14 people, including four children, were killed there, local officials said. “Today, as a birthday ‘gift’ to Putin, the Russian army destroyed a residential building in Pryluky…,” Zelenskiy said. “The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively. This was one of the most vile strikes: 70 missiles in total, many of them ballistic.” An excavator and ​dozens of rescuers with shovels sifted through rubble at the site where several sections of the five-storey building collapsed. Emergency workers used ladders to get to the upper floors of what ​remained of the building. Around 50 people were wounded, including seven children, regional officials said. BIG JUMP IN REPORTED DRONE INTERCEPTIONS Zelenskiy said six other people were killed ⁠in Kyiv, Oleksandria and Kremenchuk during the heavy overnight attack. Russia’s defence ministry said its forces had carried out a “massive strike” on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian ​regions, using high-precision land-, sea- and air-launched weapons, as well as drones. Ukraine’s air force said it had downed just over 80% of the 46 jet-powered drones launched by Russia — a ​sharp increase from recent weeks when, on average, air defences took down 50% to 60%. Since the summer, Russia has used increasing numbers of the new high-velocity drones in round-the-clock attacks on Kyiv and other cities, with Ukraine’s air defences struggling to cope with their speed. The air force did not explain the jump in the interception rate and did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Zelenskiy said the Russian ballistic missiles ​remained the major challenge for Ukraine, adding that he and his team were “every day looking for Patriot (missile interception) systems that can and must protect people’s lives”. Ukraine received a ​new €1.2 billion ($1.34 billion) tranche from the European Union on Wednesday and will channel the funds towards defence needs, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said. The US-made Patriot system is the only weapon in Ukraine’s arsenal ‌capable of ⁠stopping high-velocity ballistic missiles but tight global supplies have been drained by the Iran war as well as the Ukraine conflict. Ukraine’s energy ministry said it had started to roll out partial emergency power cuts in five Ukrainian regions due to the attacks. Russia’s defence ministry said its targets included sites where Ukrainian defence company Fire Point manufactures and stores its Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv as well as regions of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava and Kharkiv. Last week Zelenskiy said Ukraine had fired its first ​domestically made ballistic missile in combat, produced by ​Fire Point. In an interview with Reuters, he ⁠said he expected the company to have a longer-range FP-9 missile ready by the autumn. Fire Point has said that weapon will be able to reach Moscow. PEOPLE SHELTER OVERNIGHT IN KYIV METRO Zelenskiy said Ukrainian troops hit four targets in Russia over the past 24 hours, including two ​Russian oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara, and Astrakhan regions. In the Reuters interview, Zelenskiy said Ukraine would ​hit Russia’s energy assets ⁠in response to Moscow’s escalating strikes on civilian infrastructure. Many Kyiv residents took shelter in the city’s deep underground metro stations as warnings of the upcoming attacks were shared by Ukrainian officials and military intelligence. Several loud explosions reverberated through the capital during the night. “The metro is better because we live on the 9th floor of a high-rise, and it’s really scary when you’re ⁠on the ​9th floor and missiles are flying at you,” Lesia, a 49-year-old Kyiv resident, told Reuters. Ukrainian officials said ​Russian ballistic missiles as well as the drones had targeted Kyiv. Overnight air strikes on the southeastern city of Dnipro damaged an industrial facility, transport infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia and apartment buildings in Kremenchuk, regional officials said on the Telegram ​messaging app.

items.title: Edo: ADC candidate, Imansuagbon escape gun attack
items.description: BENIN CITY — The African Democratic Congress, ADC, candidate for Edo Central Senatorial District, Herberta Okonofua, and a chieftain of the party, Kenneth Imansuagbon, reportedly escaped unhurt after gunmen allegedly attacked their convoy in Igueben Local Government Area of Edo State on Tuesday. The incident reportedly occurred during political engagements by ADC leaders in the area. The party alleged that the attackers were political loyalists of the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, led by the Igueben Local Government Council Chairman, Endurance Azemegbe. However, Azemegbe denied involvement in the incident, saying he was not in Igueben when the shooting occurred and had only learnt about it from journalists. An ADC supporter, identified as Jerry Oliha, was reportedly wounded in the shooting and taken to Irrua Specialist Hospital for treatment. In a statement by its State Publicity Secretary, Chris Ojeikere, the ADC alleged that the attack was part of a wider pattern of violence against opposition members and facilities in the state. The party also cited alleged similar incidents in Etsako East, Owan West and Owan East Local Government Areas. Ojeikere alleged that the Igueben council chairman led armed men who attacked the entourage of Imansuagbon and Okonofua. He further alleged that Oliha, an ADC supporter from Ward 6, was shot at the premises of the Enogie of Igueben and was receiving medical attention at Irrua Specialist Hospital. According to him, the entourage had allegedly come under attack three times on Tuesday, first in Ward 4 and later in Ward 5 of the local government area. The party said it had informed the Divisional Police Officer, DPO, in Igueben and called for investigation into the incident. Reacting to the allegation, Azemegbe denied any involvement, saying he was not in the area when the incident occurred. “I was not around and I don’t know what happened. I am just hearing this from you. I can assure you that I will investigate the matter. I can’t say anything about what I didn’t know. The thing is strange to me. We are peaceful people and brothers in Igueben,” he said. Meanwhile, the Edo State Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Eno Ikoedem, said she could not immediately confirm the incident. She, however, said the command would wade into the matter once it was formally reported. The post Edo: ADC candidate, Imansuagbon escape gun attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CM Afridi slams Governor Kundi for 'unconstitutional' meetings, claims move intended to provoke KP govt
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Wednesday slammed Governor Faisal Karim Kundi for holding “unconstitutional” meetings, contending that the move was an “attack on democracy”. His remarks came a day after Governor Kundi chaired a meeting with the KP chief secretary and inspector general (IG) on the province’s security situation. Addressing the 60th cabinet meeting in Peshawar, Afridi said that the KP governor, who belonged to the PPP, staged a “drama” yesterday by summoning the meeting and termed the move “unconstitutional”. “The governor convening such a meeting in the presence of a provincial government with a two-thirds majority is unacceptable,” he said. “The provincial assembly, cabinet and government are fully functional and intact,” the PTI leader asserted, terming Kundi’s act an “attack on the Constitution and democracy”. Afridi contended that the purpose of the governor’s “unconstitutional activities” was to “provoke the provincial government and force it to react”. However, he advised PTI workers to stay peaceful and abide by the law and the Constitution. Calling on the province’s chief secretary and IG, the chief minister urged them not to comply with any unconstitutional or illegal order from anyone if he does not order them to do so. He reiterated that KP’s people and administration had made “countless sacrifices” in the fight against terrorism. “If someone pushes you to follow any unconstitutional order, do not follow it. It can damage our province or the country.” He also called on the chief secretary to urge the provincial administration not to indulge in any unconstitutional activity and to take action against those who were accused of corrupt practices. The chief minister then took aim at Kundi’s PPP, blaming ex-president Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, along with General Yahya Khan, for the separation of East Pakistan, now Bangladesh. He accused President Asif Ali Zardari of “intending to make another East Pakistan here“. “We will not allow any conspiracy to break up Pakistan to succeed,” he asserted. “The party that raised the slogan of democracy separated Bangladesh from Pakistan in the past for its personal interests,” he alleged. “Prioritising personal interests over national interests has been the PPP’s practice,” he further claimed. Afridi’s remarks come amid heightened tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led opposition, with the latter going ahead with its long march despite warnings from the Centre of action against any such move. Hours-long talks over the weekend between a joint delegation of the government and PPP, and the opposition alliance ended in a deadlock , with both sides blaming the other for the breakdown. Political temperatures have also remained high due to speculations of the Centre imposing governor’s rule in the province, with Kundi and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi discussing the move on Sunday. ‘Policy shift is necessary’ The KP CM also reiterated his objection to the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and defended his government’s efforts in supporting the police in the fight against terrorism. He contended that terrorism had been “imposed on the province again”, asserting that the PTI-led provincial government had always supported the police and the people of KP. Afridi maintained that he had been making efforts to strengthen the police, the Counter-Terrorism Department and Special Branch since he took the oath on Oct 15, 2025. “The KP police have the most modern weapons and equipment compared with any other police force in Pakistan,” the chief minister said. He contended that the federal government had always treated KP like a “stepchild”. “The tribal districts were merged into KP in 2018, but they have not been fully integrated financially to this day,” CM Afridi claimed, adding that the financial rights of the tribal districts agreed upon at the time of their merger had not been provided yet. The PTI leader went on to claim that federal governments had “continuously imposed military operations” on KP since 2004. “People displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies kept crying on the streets, but they have still not received full compensation,” he said, adding that nearly Rs100 billion in compensation were still outstanding. “Those whose homes were destroyed, families affected and mosques demolished are still wandering from pillar to post for their compensation.” He highlighted that while a compensation of only Rs400,000 per household had been fixed for tribal families, they had not even been paid the promised amount. Afridi stressed that a commitment was also made to provide between Rs370million and Rs380m per month to displaced people from North Waziristan at the Baka Khel camp . “The displaced people of Baka Khel are still not being provided the monthly amount as promised.” “It is the provincial government’s responsibility to stand with people displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies,” the chief minister stated, adding that his government had provided Rs21bn for displaced people. “The provincial government also has to bear responsibility for losses caused by military operations and collateral damage as a result of drone attacks,” Afridi said. He also remarked that the individuals making decisions in the federal government had no sense of the difficulties faced by the people as a result of those decisions. “If the federal government is sincere with KP, it should upgrade the province’s NFC ( National Finance Commission ) share and pay its outstanding dues of around Rs125bn to the province that has sacrificed 80,000 precious lives,” he demanded. Afridi reaffirmed that KP had to fight terrorism as well as deal with the situation created by the federal government’s policies. “The KP government and police are serious about maintaining law and order. Turning the police into personal servants and assigning them other tasks is wrong,” he declared. “If the policy of KP’s stakeholders is followed, peace can be established within 100 days,” the PTI leader insisted. He questioned why peace could not be established in the province “despite 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations over 22 years”, terming it a “failure of the federal policy”. Afridi maintained that if the issue of peace still exists in KP even after 22 years, the federal government should change its policy against terrorism if it was “serious in doing so”. “The excuse that KP is not cooperating is unacceptable; the same policy is also failing in Balochistan,” he claimed, as both provinces have witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years. “The Balochistan government is cooperating with the federal government, but peace has still not been established there,” Afridi said, claiming the Centre’s counterterrorism policy was neither effective in KP nor in Balochistan. “A shift in policy is necessary. KP can establish peace within 100 days,” he reaffirmed. In his address, Afridi also once again criticised Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s remarks that her province faced no threats from India, despite the state’s narrative of the presence of Indian proxies in Pakistan in the face of Fitna al Hindustan. Asif says ‘enough is enough’ Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif assailed the PTI-led KP government for continuing its “complete detachment from terrorism in the province and criminal indifference”. “Enough is enough!!!” he wrote in a post on X. “The PTI provincial government is roaming the streets for a so-called failed political long march, while its facilitators have unleashed a fresh wave of terrorism against the people of KP during this very time,” he said. The minister recalled Tuesday’s attacks in Dera Ismail Khan , where customs officials were among five people killed. He remarked that the entire provincial cabinet, including the chief minister, was “numb to this serious matter and fully engrossed in their politically failed long march”. “As always, these insensitive and shameless people did not even condemn the innocent murder of these five individuals in DI Khan, offered no condolences to the grieving families, did not attend their funerals or, at the very least, visit their homes to express regret,” Asif regretted. “This is inexcusable by any standard.” Instead, the defence minister noted, the KP CM had scheduled a meeting today at his party’s behest to reprimand the IG and chief secretary for attending the governor’s security meeting. “The chief minister and his cabinet of a province under the scourge of terrorism have completely abandoned the province’s people to the mercy of the terrorists. That is why the people of KP are protesting against the provincial government on the streets in various areas. “This can no longer be tolerated,” Asif declared. The defence minister accused the KP government of being in “complete collusion” with terrorists, saying there was evidence available of “its facilitator ecosystem, which every Pakistani has witnessed with their own eyes over the past three years”. Recalling past arrests of ex-premier Nawaz Sharif and his family members, as well as PML-N leaders, Asif asserted: “Time has proven that the allegations were just allegations and they were imprisoned on Imran Khan’s behest.” Yet, he stressed, the PML-N fulfilled its parliamentary role responsibly under the Constitution and did not hold the country and institutions “hostage”. “It fought a legal and constitutional battle in the courts and parliament. It did not ally with the Taliban,” Asif declared. The defence minister said that the “time has come to make crucial decisions”. “KP cannot be left any longer to the mercy of incompetent, insensitive rulers and Taliban allies,” he avowed. Asif further stressed that the unity of the country cannot be put at risk. “An entire province cannot be held hostage. Enough is enough.”

items.title: Freddie Blay accuses government of politically motivated demolitions targeting his family
items.description: Former National Chairman of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), Freddie Blay, has accused the government of using demolition exercises in parts of Accra to target its political opponents. Speaking in a yet-to-be-aired interview with JoyNews’ Elton Brobbey, Mr Blay cited the demolition of the Polo Beach Club, which he said belonged to one of his sons, as well as residential properties belonging to another son at Borteyman. He alleged that the destruction of the properties was politically motivated. “It is amazing that they can do that. They did what Israelis are doing in Gaza. What I am saying is that it is the president (John Mahama) who might have ordered it or who did it,” he said. The Polo Beach Club, located along the La beachfront near the Labadi Beach Hotel, was demolished on Friday, October 2, 2026. The operation involved personnel from the Ghana Armed Forces’ 48 Engineer Regiment and the Ghana Police Service. “The 48 Regiment Company can’t undertake movement of this nature without a nod from the national chairman of the National Security Council, thus, the president. It is dangerous,” Mr Blay said. READ ALSO: Friday’s beachfront demolition was carried out at Labadi Beach Hotel’s request, not for flood mitigation – Stan Dogbe Mr Blay’s allegations come amid controversy over the beachfront clearance and other demolition exercises in Greater Accra. However, Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Operations at the Presidency, Stan Dogbe, has given a different explanation for the Polo Beach Club demolition. In a statement on October 2, Mr Dogbe said the operation was undertaken under National Security supervision at the request of the Labadi Beach Hotel. He explained that the hotel had raised concerns about the impact of beachfront structures and commercial activities on its safety, tranquillity, reputation and visitor experience. He also clarified that the beachfront operation was separate from the government’s flood mitigation exercise, which was taking place around the Kpeshie Lagoon, East Legon Boundary Road, Oyarifa and behind Mayfair Estates.

items.title: Former Barcelona, Chelsea winger Pedro retires from football at 39
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Spanish World Cup winner and former Barcelona and Chelsea winger Pedro Rodriguez has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 39, bringing an end to a career spanning more than two decades. Pedro announced his decision in a post on social media on Wednesday, saying he was ready to begin a new chapter in his life. He wrote: “I feel that the time has come, the time to take a step forward and begin a new stage in my life. “I leave proud of having lived my dream and of all the people who were by my side to make it come true, Thank you, soccer, for making me so happy. ” Born in Tenerife, Pedro joined Barcelona’s youth academy at 17 and progressed through the club’s ranks before making his first-team debut in 2008. He became a key member of Pep Guardiola’s celebrated Barcelona side, winning three Champions League titles, five La Liga titles and an unprecedented six trophies in 2009. Pedro scored in Barcelona’s 3-1 Champions League final victory over Manchester United at Wembley in 2011 and finished his spell at the club with 99 goals in 321 appearances. He left Barcelona for Chelsea in 2015 and won the Premier League with the London club in 2017, before adding the FA Cup and Europa League in the following two seasons. He later played for Roma and Lazio, where he ended his professional career after more than 200 appearances for the Serie A club. At international level, Pedro was part of Spain’s squad that won the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa and the 2012 European Championship, earning 65 caps for Spain and scoring 17 goals. “One day, almost without believing it, I became a world champion and a starter in a World Cup final,” Pedro said in his farewell video. Reflecting on his Barcelona years, he added: “Being part of the best Barca side in history was a privilege, we won everything and amazed the world.” Barcelona also paid tribute to Pedro following his announcement, describing him as a player who “left an indelible mark” on one of the most successful periods in the club’s history. The Catalan club highlighted his journey from Tenerife to La Masia and his emergence as an important figure under Guardiola. Barcelona also recalled that Pedro became the first player to score in all six official competitions contested by the club in a single season during the 2009/10 campaign. The club said Pedro will formally mark his retirement with a farewell event at the Auditori 1899 in Barcelona on Friday, October 9, starting at 11:30am CEST. The post Former Barcelona, Chelsea winger Pedro retires from football at 39 appeared first on Vanguard News .
