items.title: Cherté de la vie : El Mansouri invitée à mettre en place un Observatoire national des prix
items.description: Après sa nomination par le Roi Mohammed VI, à la tête du nouvel exécutif à venir, Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, a été interpellée par la Fédération Nationale des Associations du Consommateur (FNAC), sur la cherté du coût de la vie. Dans une note détaillée, la FNAC lui a d'abord exprimé ses félicitations, avant de dresser une feuille de route des urgences sociales et économiques de la période à venir. L'ambition affichée est de placer la protection du pouvoir d'achat au cœur des politiques publiques, dans un contexte national marqué par une hausse persistante des coûts de la vie, la volatilité des marchés des produits de première nécessité et la mutation rapide des modes de consommation numérique. Pour l'instance consumériste, la préservation du pouvoir d'achat des ménages marocains ne doit plus faire l'objet de mesures d'urgence ponctuelles ou d'arbitrages de crise. Elle préconise au contraire la mise en place d'une politique publique globale fondée sur l'anticipation, la transparence des marchés, une régulation stricte de la concurrence et l'application effective du principe de redevabilité. Face aux hausses de prix injustifiées qui érodent le pouvoir d'achat des citoyens, la fédération plaide pour la création d'un Observatoire national des prix et du pouvoir d'achat. Conçu comme un outil d'alerte précoce fondé sur la collecte de données précises, cet organe permettrait, selon la FNAC, de cartographier en temps réel l'évolution des cours, de déceler les disparités territoriales et d'endiguer les pratiques spéculatives, les ententes illicites et la multiplication prédatrice des intermédiaires dans les circuits de distribution. Régulation du marché des carburants et refonte du cadre juridique Le marché des hydrocarbures figure au centre des préoccupations soumises à la Cheffe du gouvernement. La Fédération Nationale des Associations du Consommateur insiste sur la nécessité d'instaurer une transparence totale sur les mécanismes de fixation des prix à la pompe. La feuille de route soumise à Fatima Zahra El Mansouri exige la publication régulière et détaillée de la structure des prix finaux, incluant les coûts réels d'importation, les frais de stockage ainsi que les marges bénéficiaires nettes appliquées par les différents opérateurs de la distribution routière. Parallèlement à cette exigence de régulation sectorielle, la fédération appelle à l'actualisation et au renforcement du cadre légal régissant la protection des consommateurs, notamment à travers le développement du Droit de la consommation et le parachèvement des textes d'application de la loi 31.08. Les secteurs vitaux tels que la santé, le médicament, l'enseignement privé, les transports, l'eau, l'électricité, la téléphonie, la banque et l'assurance doivent faire l'objet d'un contrôle rigoureux de la qualité et des grilles tarifaires afin de garantir un prix juste aux usagers. Sécurité sanitaire, commerce électronique et participation institutionnelle L'analyse de la fédération met également en garde contre les dérives constatées dans les nouveaux canaux d'approvisionnement, en particulier sur les plateformes de commerce électronique et les réseaux sociaux. L'organisation insiste sur l'urgence d'étendre les mécanismes juridiques de protection aux achats en ligne afin de lutter contre la publicité mensongère, de garantir le droit de rétractation et de remboursement, et d'assurer une protection rigoureuse des données personnelles des usagers. Enfin, la note conclut sur la nécessité d'institutionnaliser le dialogue entre les pouvoirs publics et le mouvement consumériste. Considérant le citoyen comme l'acteur central du circuit économique, la fédération sollicite une implication active de la société civile dans l'élaboration et l'évaluation des politiques publiques. Il estime en ce sens qu'en renforçant l'éducation du consommateur et en soutenant le réseau des guichets de proximité, le gouvernement disposerait d'un levier concret pour restaurer la confiance des ménages dans les marchés et consolider l'équilibre économique social du Royaume. The post Cherté de la vie : El Mansouri invitée à mettre en place un Observatoire national des prix appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: La mairie de Nguidilé offre de kits scolaires à 3 552 élèves
items.description: Le maire de Nguidilé (département de Louga), Abdou Khadre Djily Lo, a procédé, lundi 05 octobre 2026, à la distribution de kits scolaires au profit de 3 552 élèves(du CI au CM2) issus des 27 écoles élémentaires publiques de la commune. Ces fournitures sont composées notamment de sacs, de cahiers et de stylos. À travers cette initiative, la municipalité entend soulager les parents d’élèves face aux dépenses liées à la rentrée scolaire. Une enveloppe de 18 millions de F CFA a ainsi été dégagée à cet effet. La cérémonie de remise s’est tenue à la salle de délibération de l’hôtel de ville, en présence des autorités administratives et académiques, des conseillers municipaux ainsi que des parents d’élèves. “Face aux charges importantes que représente la rentrée scolaire pour les familles, la municipalité a décidé d’apporter une réponse concrète”, a déclaré l’édile de Nguidilé. Selon lui, chaque élève recevra un kit scolaire comprenant un sac, des cahiers et des stylos. Outre les apprenants, la mairie de Nguidilé a également prévu d’accompagner le personnel enseignant. “Nous allons mettre à la disposition des enseignants du matériel géométrique et des rames de papier”, a indiqué le maire. Dans la même dynamique, il a annoncé qu’une enveloppe de 250 000 francs CFA sera remise aux enseignants sous forme de subvention. Cette contribution vise à les accompagner dans la préparation et l’organisation des évaluations collectives au niveau de la commune. Les autorités académiques ainsi que le collectif des chefs d’établissement ont vivement salué les efforts consentis par la municipalité en faveur de l’éducation. Falel PAM (Correspondant)

items.title: Ghana targets rice self-sufficiency by 2028 as government secures $18.8m AfDB grant
items.description: Ghana is targeting full self-sufficiency in rice production by 2028 as the government steps up efforts to close the country’s 44% rice supply gap. Minister of Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku, says the government is targeting total paddy rice production of 3.31 million metric tonnes by 2028, with the aim of ending the country’s reliance on rice imports. Speaking at a press briefing on the Regional West African Resilient Rice Value Chains Project, the Minister said Ghana’s rice production has increased significantly, but local output remains insufficient to meet national demand. “Rice is now Ghana’s second most important area after maize. Population growth, urbanization, and changing consumer preferences have pushed demand well ahead of what we produce,” Mr Opoku said. According to him, milled rice production increased from about 650,000 tonnes in 2024 to 960,000 tonnes in 2025. Despite the increase, he said local production currently meets only about 56% of national demand, leaving about 44% to be supplied through imports. “This gap comes at a cost. Ghana spends approximately 500 million US dollars every year on rice imports. That is money that could be earned by Ghanaian farmers, millers, and traders,” he said. The Minister said the government is determined to close the production gap within the next two years. “Our national target is to become self-sufficient in rice by 2028, just two years ahead of us, with total paddy production of 3.31 million metric tons,” he said. The government is also leveraging an $18.8 million grant from the African Development Bank (AfDB) under the Regional West African Resilient Rice Value Chains Project, known as REWARD, to support the rice sector. Mr Opoku stressed that the funding is a grant and not a loan. “We have received 18.8 million dollars for the development of our rice value chain, and this is a grant. It’s not a loan. A grant from the African Development Bank ,” he said. The project will support policy and regulatory reforms, develop 3,200 hectares of land for rice production in the northern savanna ecological zone and improve access to quality seeds and mechanisation. The intervention will also provide farm machinery, improve rice processing centres, reduce post-harvest losses and strengthen links between farmers, markets and the private sector. The project is expected to reach more than 20,000 smallholder farmers across selected districts, while creating opportunities for aggregators, processors and service providers. Mr Opoku said the initiative forms part of the government’s broader Feed Ghana programme. “REWARD is Feed Ghana in action for rice. It is a deliberate intervention in the rice value chain to raise local output and reduce the national import bill,” he said. The Minister said rice produced under the project will also help supply schools, prisons and other public institutions with quality locally produced rice.

items.title: What Aaron Sorkin Forgot About The Social Network
items.description: The Social Network was powered by alienation. David Fincher’s incredible 2010 film, written by Aaron Sorkin, tells the story of an internet age. It does this through the fraught relationship between two frustrated college students, hungry for popularity and connection, one of whom just happens to be Mark Zuckerberg. It’s a haunted movie that did an outstanding job predicting the nightmares that awaited us in our lives online. Now comes a sequel of sorts: The Social Reckoning , written and directed by Sorkin, which amounts to a long and drawn-out “Told ya so!” What’s powering The Social Reckoning is outrage—and that outrage is certainly justified. Set from 2019 to 2021, it dramatizes a series of Wall Street Journal articles that exposed the company’s willful ignorance, and oftentimes algorithmic encouragement, of Facebook’s damages to society. Sorkin diligently lays out the reporting by Jeff Horwitz (played by Jeremy Allen White), the investigative journalist who collaborated with the product manager turned whistleblower Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison) to reveal the company’s misdeeds; there’s no disputing the public good of their work. But Sorkin’s enterprise has very little excitement to it and instead feels like a perfunctory coda to a point he made more poetically many years ago. Part of the problem, undoubtedly, lies with the director. After spending decades among Hollywood’s most reliable and colorful screenwriters, Sorkin made the leap to filmmaking in 2017 with the solid biographical thriller Molly’s Game . He’s made three movies since, each a rendition of real-life events told with his distinctively bouncy, elliptical, rat-a-tat dialogue. His visuals, however, have never matched the liveliness of his writing. The Social Reckoning is disappointingly flat and gray, set in anodyne hotel rooms and glassy offices, and unbearably static. In The Social Network , Fincher made the Harvard campus that Zuckerberg skulked around feel both dreamy and hostile; Sorkin has no such impression of the Silicon Valley walled city that the Facebook co-founder ended up in. [ Read: How Facebook fails 90 percent of its users ] One of the biggest diminishments between the two films, though, is the lack of any emotional turmoil at The Social Reckoning ’s center. The prior entry depicts the inception of Facebook and, just as important, the love-hate friendship Zuckerberg had with his co-founder Eduardo Saverin—two socially stunted buddies who become rivals after the silly college website they created takes off. Reckoning offers nothing so tumultuous or compelling; the only interpersonal tension stems from how Horwitz (whom White plays as deadpan, a bit old-fashioned, and consummately professional) tries to make Haugen feel comfortable about leaking internal documents. Although the nervous Haugen sometimes teases the reporter for his lack of tech know-how, their banter never even rises to a sizzle. The other unavoidable comparison point between the original movie and the sequel is Zuckerberg himself. Eisenberg’s nervy performance in The Social Network made him an Oscar-nominated star, and it’s clear from how the part is written here that Sorkin expected him to return (indeed, he’s said as much ). Eisenberg has been replaced by Jeremy Strong, who’s appeared in two other Sorkin projects, and the Succession actor tackles the role with his usual aplomb ; he does a fine imitation of Zuckerberg’s stiff and pitchy voice. But though Eisenberg’s rendition of the 20-something CEO buzzes with youthful insecurity, Strong’s Zuckerberg, here in his late 30s, is almost zombified. The character is always seen sitting or stiffly standing, and has no light behind his eyes. That the head of one of the biggest tech companies in the world has become somewhat ghoulish and surrounded by yes-men is easy to believe yet hardly shocking; when Zuckerberg appears on-screen, the audience is meant to boo and hiss until he exits. It is simply not enough for The Social Reckoning to present the facts that Facebook misled its users and encouraged many of their worst impulses. Those revelations are patiently explained by Haugen and Horwitz over and over again, as they emphasize to each other how the website’s algorithms pushed outrageous material that nudged its users toward hate groups to keep them scrolling. But the viewer can already learn about these developments by reading the existing source material. [ Read: One way The Social Network got Facebook right ] That Sorkin relies on his favorite screenwriting tropes, which have grown creakier and creakier, doesn’t help—and they feel especially tired as he tackles subjects this topical. Attempts at witty repartee about such subjects as the musical Show Boat and Frank Capra movies fall flat coming out of White’s and Madison’s mouths. The narrative also hops backwards and forwards in time, encompassing the coronavirus pandemic and the January 6 insurrection, which just feels choppy and unfocused; Sorkin’s hammer-blow point about Facebook encouraging humanity’s worst impulses in regard to both crises can be seen coming from a mile off. The Social Reckoning isn’t wrong about the troubled world Facebook has helped make. The film just can’t talk about it in a remotely interesting way.

items.title: Israelis mark three years since October 7 as Palestinians mourn Gaza’s destruction
items.description: Israelis gathered in silence on Wednesday in a ​kibbutz near the Gaza border that was overrun by Hamas militants on October 7 three years ago, mourning victims of attacks that set off Israel’s assault in ‌Gaza and plunged the Middle East into war. In the Gaza Strip, devastated by two years of Israeli bombardment, Palestinians sheltering among the ruins of destroyed cities recalled life before a war that displaced nearly the entire population and tore apart families. The attacks of October 7, 2023, were the deadliest day in Israel’s history. Militants led by Hamas killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages, a cross-border incursion that traumatised Israelis who have demanded government accountability. Israel’s subsequent ​bombardment and ground operations in Gaza have killed more than 74,000 people, including at least 1,400 killed in the past year since a US-brokered ceasefire, which halted major fighting ​but has failed to stop Israeli attacks or secure the disarmament of Hamas. ‘A VERY DIFFICULT DAY’ In Kfar Aza, where Hamas militants killed dozens of ⁠Israelis before taking 19 hostages back into Gaza, residents held a vigil for those killed, standing in silence as a trumpet played a solemn bugle call. A resident read out a ​roll call of the dead. Zion Regev, a community leader in the kibbutz, said most residents remain displaced and have yet to return, the trauma of October 7 continuing to shape their lives. “This ​is the first time we are doing all the things here in the kibbutz,” Regev said of the vigil. “It’s a very emotional day, it’s a very difficult day for our community, three years after October 7th.” Elsewhere in Israel, protesters against what they view as a lack of accountability for the security failure gathered outside parliament in Jerusalem, blaming Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for refusing an independent inquiry into the attack. Some protesters held signs reading: “The ​people will remember October 7 on October 27,” a reference to an Israeli general election 20 days away that is being viewed as a referendum on Netanyahu’s long tenure in power. “We ​need the change and we need hope and we need to know that we have a government that cares about the public and doesn’t work also only for themselves,” said protester Shaked Arrad. Netanyahu has rejected ‌blame for ⁠the security breach and resisted calls for an independent investigation. That has frustrated many in Israel, including families of those killed in the attacks, some of whom have joined the election race. On the eve of the anniversary, he told a cabinet meeting that Israelis “remember with grief and pain our heroes who fell in the War of Redemption and our brothers and sisters who fell in the terrible massacre in the Gaza border communities”. Election polls show neither Netanyahu nor his main competitors would muster enough seats in parliament to form a coalition if a vote were held today. DISPLACED GAZANS ​RECALL LIFE BEFORE ISRAELI ASSAULT The anniversary is the ​first since the October 10, 2025, ceasefire ⁠deal, which has left Israel in control of around two-thirds of Gaza, where it has demolished remaining buildings and ordered residents out. Hamas controls the remaining third of the territory, a narrow strip on the coast where the 2 million population mostly live in makeshift tents and bombed-out buildings. In the latest violence, Gaza medics said on Wednesday Israel’s military had ​carried out air strikes in Beit Lahia in northern Gaza and in Khan Younis in the south, killing at least two Palestinians and ​wounding others. The Israeli ⁠military said it had struck a militant target in Beit Lahia, without providing details. It did not immediately provide comment on the strike in Khan Younis. Umm Mohammad, a mother of five displaced from Gaza City and now living with her husband and children in a tent encampment in Deir Al-Balah, said the war had ripped her family apart. “We were one happy family. The war displaced us. My son ⁠left Gaza, ​the other went to a separate tent, my daughters left with their husbands to other parts of the Strip ​and we rarely meet,” she said. On this day, she said, “we recall how happy, despite all problems, we were before the war broke out, destroying everything we loved.”

items.title: Support constitutional amendment to fix voting day on Tuesday – Asiedu Nketiah urges SDA Church
items.description: National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has urged the Seventh-day Adventist (SDA) Church and other religious bodies to support a constitutional amendment to permanently fix Tuesdays for presidential and parliamentary elections. He said fixing a weekday for national elections would help prevent recurring disputes between political parties, the Electoral Commission (EC) and religious groups whenever an election date coincided with an important day of worship. Mr Asiedu Nketiah made the call at the centenary celebration of the SDA Church at Sekyedumase in the Ejura-Sekyedumase Municipality of the Ashanti Region. He recalled that ahead of the 2024 general election, both the SDA Church and the Saviour Church of Ghana had appealed to him to support their calls for the EC to move the election from Saturday, December 7, 2024, which coincided with the Sabbath observed by Seventh-day Adventists. He said similar concerns had been raised by Muslim and other Christian communities in previous elections when polling dates coincided with Friday and Sunday, respectively. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said the recurring situation created an unnecessary conflict between citizens’ constitutional right to vote and their religious obligations. He therefore urged the SDA Church and other religious bodies to support efforts towards amending the Constitution to establish Tuesday as the fixed voting day. “I urge the leadership of the SDA Church and other religious bodies to push for this amendment to avoid needless arguments among political parties, the Electoral Commission and affected religious bodies whenever a voting day falls on the day of worship of any of the major religions in Ghana,” he said. Under the current constitutional framework, the EC has the authority to determine the date for presidential and parliamentary elections within the periods prescribed by the Constitution. Ghana’s general elections have, by convention, been held on December 7 every four years. The 2024 election date generated particular concern because December 7 fell on a Saturday. The EC subsequently maintained the date after considering the applicable legal framework and electoral arrangements. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said a fixed weekday would provide a more predictable arrangement and reduce the likelihood of religious considerations becoming a recurring source of disagreement during election periods.

items.title: Crise du carburant : les réserves pétrolières occidentales sont presque épuisées
items.description: Les reserves de petrole disponibles dans les pays occidentaux ont ete epuisees en raison de la guerre menee par les etats-Unis contre l'Iran, a rapporte Bloomberg le 6 octobre, citant Russell Hardy, directeur general de Vitol. Le plus grand negociant independant de petrole au monde s'est exprime lors du forum Energy Intelligence a Londres. Commentant la decision des pays du G7 de liberer 100 millions de barils de petrole et de gazole provenant de leurs reserves strategiques, Hardy a souligne que les details precis de cette decision « ne sont pas tout a fait transparents ». Le dirigeant de Vitol a egalement averti que la situation tendue sur le marche des produits petroliers devrait perdurer au cours des prochains mois. La veille, Amin Nasser, directeur general de Saudi Aramco, le fournisseur de petrole brut, avait averti lors du meme evenement que les reserves mondiales de petrole, qui permettent de compenser les interruptions d'approvisionnement, etaient « effroyablement faibles » , ce qui risque d'aggraver la situation sur le marche si la navigation dans le detroit d'Ormuz n'est pas entierement retablie. Selon lui, sur les quelque 6 milliards de barils que comptent les reserves mondiales de petrole, moins de 10 % sont en realite accessibles en raison de diverses contraintes logistiques. Quant a l'initiative des pays du G7, Amin Nasser a souligne que cette decision, tout en permettant de gagner du temps, ne resoudra pas le desequilibre entre l'offre et la demande. Selon lui, meme apres le retablissement de la navigation dans le detroit d'Ormuz, les pays consommateurs d'energie pourraient avoir besoin de jusqu'a deux ans pour reconstituer leurs stocks. Crise energetique sur fond d'impasse au Moyen-Orient Fin septembre, Reuters a indique que les stocks de petrole brut de la Reserve strategique de petrole (SPR) des etats-Unis avaient baisse a 283,8 millions de barils. D'apres les donnees du ministere americain de l'energie, il s'agit du niveau le plus bas depuis octobre 1982 . Cette baisse des stocks est liee a la mise en œuvre d'une decision prise en mars 2026, prevoyant la mise a disposition de jusqu'a 172 millions de barils de petrole provenant de la SPR dans le cadre d'operations d'echange. Les entreprises devront en contrepartie restituer le petrole recu, majore d'un volume supplementaire. En Europe, les stocks de carburant ont egalement atteint leur plus bas niveau depuis 2022, dans un contexte de reduction des approvisionnements en provenance du Moyen-Orient. a la mi-septembre, les stocks mondiaux de gazole etaient en baisse depuis plus de six mois. Les compagnies petrolieres americaines y ont vu le debut d'une « grande crise du carburant » . Dans le meme temps, la situation au Moyen-Orient ne se denoue toujours pas : les etats-Unis et l'Iran ne parviennent a s'entendre ni sur les termes d'un accord de paix ni sur la question de la reouverture du detroit d'Ormuz. Le 25 septembre, le president americain Donald Trump a rejete la proposition de l'Iran visant a rouvrir le detroit, proposition transmise par Teheran par l'intermediaire de mediateurs en marge de l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies a New York. Selon le president du Parlement iranien, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, les conditions d'ouverture d'une voie maritime cle comprennent la levee du blocus maritime americain, le degel de ses avoirs, la fin des sanctions sur ses exportations petrolieres, l'arret des operations militaires americaines, le retrait de forces americaines autour de ses frontieres ainsi que des compensations pour les dommages subis. L'Iran exige egalement la fin des attaques contre le pays et ses allies regionaux.

items.title: FG releases 8-month consolidated allowance to non-academic staff
items.description: …moves to avert fresh crisis in tertiary institutions By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has released eight months’ arrears of the Consolidated Non-Academic Staff Tertiary Institutions Allowance, CONTA, to non-academic workers in federal universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, in a move aimed at strengthening industrial harmony and preventing disruptions in the nation’s tertiary education system. The allowance, covering January to August 2026, was announced by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, on Wednesday, barely two days after the government commenced payment of the Consolidated Academic Tertiary Institutions Allowance, CATA, to academic staff. The twin payments signal the Federal Government’s efforts to address staff welfare concerns across the tertiary education sector and ease tensions that could threaten the stability of the academic calendar. Alausa said the release of CONTA demonstrated the administration’s commitment to workers’ welfare and recognition of the critical role played by non-academic personnel in keeping tertiary institutions functional. According to him, the welfare and motivation of both academic and non-academic staff remained central to ensuring stable institutions and producing the skilled manpower required for national development. He said the payment was also part of the Federal Government’s broader efforts to address legitimate welfare concerns, promote industrial harmony and minimise disruptions to academic activities nationwide. The minister said the administration would continue to strengthen institutions responsible for developing Nigeria’s human capital, stressing that a stable tertiary education system was essential to the country’s socio-economic development. Alausa further assured stakeholders that the Federal Ministry of Education would sustain consultations with relevant unions, heads of institutions and other stakeholders to resolve outstanding issues and build a more stable and productive tertiary education system. He appealed for continued cooperation from academic and non-academic staff, institutional authorities and unions as the government implements its reforms in the sector. The minister reiterated that the ministry under his leadership would continue to prioritise staff welfare, institutional stability, human capital development and improved learning outcomes. He added that the Federal Government remained committed to fulfilling its obligations to personnel in the tertiary education sector and addressing outstanding welfare issues in line with the human capital development objectives of the Renewed Hope Agenda. items.title: ‘It’s a systemic problem’ – All Black PRO dismisses Kurt’s resignation calls
items.description: Communications Director for Swedru All Blacks, Nathaniel Obeng believes demanding the resignation of Ghana Football Association (GFA) President, Kurt Okraku, will not fix the ongoing crisis surrounding the Black Stars. Calls for Kurt to step down have intensified among fans and key stakeholders following Ghana’s shocking home defeat to The Gambia in the 2027 AFCON qualifiers. The loss came right after the senior national team suffered an opening-match defeat against Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké. “My personal view is that if we personalise this situation, we’ve been here before. There was a whole campaign to get somebody out, the person was ousted, a new person came, and now we are complaining about the same thing,” Obeng stated. “So, it might be that it is not an individual problem; it’s a systemic problem. I believe getting Kurt Okraku out won’t solve the issue. It is a system problem.” The Black Stars currently sit bottom of Group C without a single point, while Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia lead the standings with six points each. The coaching seat also remains vacant after former Portuguese manager Carlos Queiroz mutually parted ways with the GFA following the Gambia defeat. The Black Stars are set to return in November for a crucial doubleheader against Somalia at the Accra Sports Stadium.

items.title: Senior English football figures fear Man City could play in next season’s UCL despite relegation
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senior figures within English football are concerned that Manchester City could still play in next season’s Champions League even if the club is relegated from the Premier League over financial breaches, according to the BBC. The concern centres on a possible scenario in which City win the Champions League this season, which would give them a route into next season’s competition as defending champions regardless of their position in the English football pyramid. BBC Sport reports that there is currently no automatic mechanism to prevent a club from competing in a European competition if it qualifies on sporting merit. An independent commission recently found City guilty of all charges relating to the inflation of sponsorship revenue by £830 million through sham contracts, as well as concealing another £90 million in expenses. The commission found that without the alleged breaches, City would have failed the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules in all nine seasons between 2009-10 and 2017-18. City have denied any wrongdoing and described the verdict as a “Premier League conspiracy”. The club has appealed the findings. BBC Sport said several senior figures in the English game had raised concerns about City potentially qualifying for the Champions League next season if their appeal fails and they receive severe sanctions. Such sanctions could include a heavy points deduction, a large fine, transfer restrictions or even immediate expulsion from the Premier League. One of the immediate issues is whether City would be granted the UEFA licence required to compete in European competitions. The licence process is handled by the Football Association and delegated to the Premier League, but the criteria are based largely on a club’s current financial position and do not take historical breaches or sanctions into account. One source told BBC Sport that the issue of City’s licence “had been raised”, adding that resolving it would require “the sort of joined up thinking that’s been a bit lacking so far”. Another source said the grounds for refusing City a licence were unclear because licences are awarded based on current financial performance. Even if a points deduction prevents City from qualifying for the Champions League through their Premier League position, they could potentially qualify by winning the competition itself. There are also other European routes. Winning the FA Cup could secure a place in the Europa League, while victory in the Carabao Cup would provide a route into the Conference League. UEFA cannot take action while the Premier League’s disciplinary process is ongoing, but its administration and Club Financial Control Body are expected to consider possible scenarios. UEFA could open a disciplinary case to find a way of removing City’s eligibility if the club’s appeal fails and they qualify for Europe. However, there are concerns over whether such action would succeed after City previously overturned a two-year UEFA ban at the Court of Arbitration for Sport in 2020. The CAS ruled at the time that UEFA’s findings against City were time-barred under its rules. The Premier League’s sanctioning hearing, which will determine the punishment for the latest findings, has yet to be scheduled. items.title: Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
items.description: US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran ​must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how ‌Tehran makes decisions in negotiations. Vance, a longtime skeptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart. The war has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for President Donald Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections. Speaking on Monday after a campaign trip in Alaska, Vance said ​any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future nuclear drawdowns. “If you don’t want a nuclear weapon, then why ​do you need 60% enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don’t build highly enriched ⁠fuel. That’s a very basic threshold issue,” Vance said. “I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their ​enrichment capacity.” Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran’s ​latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterms. Vance said the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions. “We’re not going to trade words for actions,” Vance said. UNCLEAR HOW IRAN MAKES DECISIONS: VANCE Complicating matters, Vance said Washington is uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran. Vance said the US was in talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. But ​it was unclear how much authority they wield within Iran’s power structure, he said, after joint US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. “One ​of the things we picked up on is it’s not totally clear how their country makes decisions,” Vance said. Separately, Trump said on Tuesday his “biggest problem” is no one knows who is running Iran. Iran’s ‌Foreign Ministry ⁠spokesperson said on Sunday that US officials are well aware of who their Iranian counterparts are and how Iran’s decision-making system works. “The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials,” Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference. Vance told Reuters he has held personal conversations with field commanders to gauge battlefield conditions. He dismissed concerns over critical munitions shortages and added that while Iranian troops are periodically able to strike commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, they are largely unable to prevent energy exports through ​the waterway. Vance declined to say if he ​was leading peace talks, though he is ⁠frequently cited as the White House’s top negotiator. “We’re certainly involved,” he said. “Ultimately, the president of the United States is driving things.” The war — and its $3 billion monthly price tag — has become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the ​defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress. Vance has sought to temper criticism of Trump’s handling of the conflict, telling ​voters they should not ⁠let that issue keep them from backing Republicans in next month’s elections. In Alaska, Vance rallied for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is locked in a tight reelection battle with Democratic challenger Mary Peltola. Trump carried Alaska by 13 percentage points in 2024, but rising everyday costs have put the state in play. Before speaking with Reuters, Vance focused much of his speech on affordability concerns, especially around ⁠energy. Alaska’s remote ​locale makes consumer goods more expensive, and energy production is a key industry. Rally attendees roared when Sullivan nearly ​introduced Vance as the president of the US, rather than the vice president. Vance is seen as a leading Republican contender to succeed Trump in the White House. Vance told Reuters afterward that he had not decided whether to ​seek the presidency in 2028. “I’m inherently a procrastinator,” he said. “I really haven’t thought about it much.”

items.title: Killings: Drop your ambition now, northern Islamic clerics tell Tinubu
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Over 1,000 northern Islamic clerics have told President Bola Tinubu to drop his 2027 re-election ambition, citing killings, kidnappings and acts of terrorism across the country, particularly in the North-West. The demand was contained in a communique issued at the end of a national conference on “An Assessment of the State of the Nation under President Tinubu and the 2027 General Elections,” held in Kano State on Sunday. The conference was organised by the clerics under the umbrella of “Ko Da Naka”, an organization which says it is dedicated to “the Struggle to Promote Good Governance and Community Development”, in collaboration with AFAQ Educational Foundation. Some of the clerics who presented papers at the conference included Dr Abdulmuɗɗalib Ahmad Giɗaɗo, Prof Muhd Muslim Ibrahim, Sheikh Kabir Bashir Abdulhamid, Dr Aminu Isma’il Sagagi, Dr Najibullah Abdallah Nuhu and Sheikh Abdurrazaq Uba Musa. Others were Sheikh Musa Muhd Ɗan kwano, Brr El-Zubair, Dr Yahuza Getso, Prof Ibrahim Siraj Adhama, Dr Umar Dokaji and Sheikh Muhd Sani Khamis (Abu Haisam). “Alternatively, the President should refrain from contesting the 2027 election. If he refuses to do so, it is incumbent upon citizens to reject his candidacy and allow those whom they believe can provide better leadership,” the communique said. The communique noted that following lectures and extensive deliberations on security, economy, migration of skilled professionals from the country, role of religious scholars in standing for truth, and the 2027 general elections, the approximately one thousand participants at the conference, reached the conclusion. The clerics called on the government to take urgent action to address insecurity in the Northwest and other affected parts of the country. They said if the administration fails to do so, citizens should reject Tinubu’s candidacy and give an opportunity to leaders they believe can provide better leadership. They also faulted the government’s economic policies, which they said had deepened the hardship of ordinary Nigerians. The policies they named include the removal of the fuel subsidy, changes to the naira exchange-rate system, increases in electricity tariffs and tax reforms. “It is unfortunate that the government has continued to insist on pursuing these policies, which are increasing hardship among the people, rather than reviewing and correcting them. “The government prioritised the growth of its revenue at a time when the rising cost of living and unemployment are threatening the lives and well-being of citizens”, they said. According to the clerics, participants at the conference “unanimously agreed that it would be inappropriate to re-elect this government in the forthcoming 2027 general elections if it does not change its harmful economic policies.” The clerics also expressed grave concern over the continuing departure of Nigerian doctors, teachers, engineers and other skilled professionals. They linked the exodus to unemployment, inadequate facilities, poor working conditions and the country’s difficult economic situation. They urged the government to improve salaries, working conditions and professional development, and to create opportunities that would encourage skilled Nigerians abroad to return home. The clerics urged religious scholars to speak truth to power, defend justice and refuse to become political instruments. According to them, scholars should praise what is good and criticise what is wrong, regardless of the party, tribe or religion of the person in power. They asked Nigerians to put the country’s future above party, ethnic and regional interests, and to assess candidates by their experience, integrity, competence and policies. “Nigerians should not be asked to endure another term of the same policies while families struggle to meet basic needs and the promised relief remains out of reach,” the communique said. items.title: Mahama orders sanctions for officials who fail to enforce building safety rules
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has directed the Minister of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, to ensure that officials responsible for enforcing building safety regulations are held accountable when structural failures occur. He said officials tasked with ensuring the safety of buildings must be identified and sanctioned if they fail to properly enforce the relevant regulations. President Mahama made the remarks on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, at the National Conference on Housing Finance, where he called for stronger enforcement of building regulations at the district assembly level. He expressed concern about buildings continuing to be constructed despite stop-work orders issued by local authorities, insisting that such directives must be enforced. “More often than not, you see red paint stop work, and yet the work continues. And you wonder what’s happening,” President Mahama said. “And one day they are working, and the whole house comes tumbling down. You ask, who gave the permit for that building?” The President said accountability must be established whenever a building collapses, particularly where regulatory officials failed to perform their duties. “These are things that the Ministry of Local Government should take very seriously. If a house collapses, we must see whose duty it was to ensure that that house was safe, and that person must be sanctioned for it,” he said. President Mahama said the issue must be addressed at the district assembly level, where building permits are issued and compliance with safety requirements is monitored. His comments come amid concerns over structural failures in Ghana, with more than 75 building collapses estimated to have been recorded across the country over the past five years, while an estimated one to three multi-storey building failures occur annually. Beyond building safety, President Mahama called for broader measures to improve housing conditions, including tackling overcrowding in slums, insecure land tenure, poor sanitation and inadequate access to utilities. “We must also ensure that the homes we build are safe, accessible and connected to jobs and essential services,” he said.

items.title: No eligible voter must be left behind – INEC
items.description: ,,,INEC, Canada, IFES deepen inclusive voter education The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has commenced a national training programme aimed at strengthening inclusive voter education ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC disclosed this in a statement posted on its X platform on Wednesday, saying the two-day National Inclusive Voter Education Training was designed to equip its Gender and Inclusivity staff with the skills required to reach citizens with diverse needs. The training, supported by the Government of Canada through its Fund for Local Initiatives and organised in collaboration with the International Foundation for Electoral Systems, IFES, is being held at the Exclusive Serene Hotel, Wuye, Abuja. The programme brought together staff of INEC’s Gender and Inclusivity Department from the states and other relevant personnel, with emphasis on practical approaches to ensuring that voter information reaches and can be understood by all categories of eligible citizens. The initiative is part of the commission’s efforts to promote a free, fair, credible, transparent and inclusive electoral process ahead of the 2027 elections. INEC said its commitment to inclusion had also been reflected in recent engagements with the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities, JONAPWD, Organisations of Persons with Disabilities, OPDs, and other stakeholders to strengthen the participation of persons with disabilities in the elections. Speaking at the training, First Secretary, Political Affairs, High Commission of Canada in Nigeria, Colton Bridges, said Canada considered inclusive elections and democratic processes important components of democratic development. Bridges welcomed participants and expressed appreciation to IFES for its contribution to the initiative. He said the project was funded through Canada’s Fund for Local Initiatives and was one of several election-related projects being supported by the Canadian government as preparations for the 2027 general election intensify. According to him, the decision to focus on inclusion reflected Canada’s commitment to ensuring that democratic and electoral processes were accessible to all citizens. “I hope for the next two days, what you’re going to take away from it is maybe how to do it a little bit better, how to do it differently, some strategies you can use to ensure that your education is inclusive,” he said. Bridges, who said he had participated in election observation missions in Ondo, Anambra and Osun states, said the experiences had enabled him to witness some of INEC’s efforts to promote inclusive elections, particularly for persons with disabilities. He, however, stressed that electoral inclusion should extend beyond disability. He identified people who do not speak English fluently, persons with limited literacy, residents of remote communities and citizens without internet access among those who may require specific approaches to voter education. “People who need specific types of information or specific types of messaging” must be reached to enable them to participate fully in the electoral process, he said. On persons with disabilities, Bridges acknowledged that some of the challenges they face, including access to education and employment, extend beyond INEC’s mandate. He stressed, however, that the commission had the responsibility and capacity to ensure that the electoral process itself was accessible to persons with disabilities, enabling them to vote and exercise their franchise. The training is expected to strengthen the capacity of INEC personnel to deliver voter education that takes into account the different circumstances and needs of eligible voters ahead of the 2027 elections. items.title: Court grants bail to banker accused of stealing GH¢1 million
items.description: A 28-year-old banker has appeared before the Adenta Circuit Court for allegedly stealing GH¢1 million from a community bank. Adjetey Isaac Noi, the Branch Manager of Oyibi Area Community Bank PLC, is accused of reactivating a dormant customer account and using it as a transit account to transfer funds to various accounts in different banks. The alleged offence occurred between March and September 2025. Noi has been charged with stealing. He pleaded not guilty. The court, presided over by Mrs Angela Attachie, granted him bail in the sum of GH¢1 million with two sureties. The sureties are required to justify the bail with landed property. Defence counsel prayed for bail, arguing that the accused was not a flight risk because he has a fixed place of abode at Dodowa in the Greater Accra Region. The case has been adjourned to February 17, 2027. Presenting the facts, Chief Inspector Maxwell Lanyo said the complainant was the Head of Audit and Inspection at ARB Apex Bank PLC, while the accused served as Branch Manager of Oyibi Area Community Bank PLC. On September 28, 2026, the prosecution said the complainant and a team of auditors conducted an audit and inspection of the Oyibi branch following intelligence that fraudulent transactions were being carried out there. During the exercise, the auditors allegedly detected a transfer of GH¢1 million from the bank’s internal account into account number 3061110010021221, held in the name of Nii Adjei Sowatey, at the same bank. The audit team immediately informed the bank’s head office, which directed the complainant to lodge an official complaint with the police. The prosecution said Noi was subsequently arrested but failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for the transfer of the funds during police interrogation. Investigations, the court heard, revealed that the accused allegedly reactivated the dormant account without the account holder’s consent and used it as a transit account to channel the funds to various accounts in other banks. Noi was unable to account for the transfers during investigations, the prosecution said.

items.title: We have a winning team for 2028 – NPP Atwima Nwabiagya South Secretary
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) Secretary for Atwima Nwabiagya South Constituency in the Ashanti Region, John Kwame Duodu, popularly known as Sir John, has expressed strong confidence in the newly elected national executives of the party, saying they have what it takes to lead the party’s comeback to power in the 2028 general elections. According to him, the team elected at the just-ended National Delegates Conference is solid, experienced, and capable of reorganizing the party at all levels to recapture power from the National Democratic Congress (NDC). Mr. Duodu made the remarks in a statement issued shortly after the conference, which was held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi and brought together thousands of delegates from across the country. He said the conference was a clear demonstration of internal democracy within the NPP and a testament to the party’s commitment to strong structures and collective leadership. “The delegates have spoken, and they have given us a solid team. I have strong belief in the newly elected executives. They have the experience, the grassroots connection and the commitment needed to reorganize and energize the Elephant family for victory in 2028,” he stated. Mr. Duodu, who leads the party’s administrative work in Atwima Nwabiagya South, one of the NPP’s strongholds in the Ashanti Region, congratulated all winners of the National Delegates Conference, describing their victory as a reflection of the trust and confidence reposed in them by party delegates. He noted that their diverse backgrounds and track record in party work position them well to reconcile factions, bridge gaps and build a formidable front ahead of the next elections. “This solid team will lead the NPP’s bounce back to power. I have strong belief in their capacity to unite the party, reconnect with the base and rebrand our message to Ghanaians ahead of 2028,” he stressed. He also extended words of encouragement to aspirants who contested but were unsuccessful, urging them not to see the outcome as the end of the road but as part of the democratic process. He appealed to them to remain committed, dedicated, and actively involved in party activities, particularly in mobilization and campaign efforts towards 2028. “To all those who could not make it, I urge you to continue to be committed to party activities. The NPP needs every hand on deck, especially as we prepare for the 2028 general elections. Your contribution is still crucial,” he said. Mr. Duodu further called on both winners and losers to put the contest behind them and work together in unity and with a common purpose. He emphasized that unity will be the NPP’s greatest asset as it seeks to return to power. He urged party faithful in Atwima Nwabiagya South and across the country, from polling station executives to national leadership, to rally behind the new executives, support their vision and work tirelessly to reposition the party, regain public trust and secure victory in 2028. “The journey to 2028 has started. We must forgive each other, unite and channel all our energies into making the NPP attractive again to Ghanaians,” he added.

items.title: Taïba Ndiaye : 17,8 millions pour la rentrée et un lycée au nom du president Ale Lo
items.description: La commune de Taïba Ndiaye a mobilisé une enveloppe de 17 815 000 F CFA pour la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, a annoncé le 06 octobre 2026 son maire, Assane Ndiaye.Il s'exprimait lors de la cérémonie officielle de remise de fournitures scolaires aux 18 écoles élémentaires de la commune, en présence de l'inspecteur chef du district de Mboro, Ibrahima Diabaté, de l'adjoint au sous prefet de Meouane, des autorites locales et directeurs d'ecoles. « L'importance de cette cérémonie, c'est d'investir aujourd'hui pour récolter demain. Aujourd'hui ce sont les élèves, demain ce seront les adultes », a déclaré le maire.Selon lui, la dotation vise à soulager les parents d'élèves en milieu rural confrontés à des difficultés pour l'achat des furniture. Le college et le lycee ont egalement recu leur part.L'enveloppe comprend, outre les fournitures, 124 poches d'encre pour les photocopieuses de dernière génération offertes l'an dernier aux 18 écoles élémentaires par la commune. Le maire a également annoncé un projet d'acquisition de tables-bancs pour faire face à l'afflux d'élèves en classe de sixième, consécutif à la suppression du concours d'entrée en sixième. Avec ce projet, l'investissement global devrait atteindre 20 millions de F CFA, a-t-il précisé. Assane Ndiaye a invité les parents à libérer les élèves, actuellement retenus par les travaux champêtres, en cette période de récolte, afin qu'ils rejoignent les classes dès l'ouverture, sous le thème « Ubbi tey, jàng tey ». Assane s'est rejoui de la participation du parc eolien a la remise de fournitures scolaires, dans Le cadre du RSE. Par ailleurs, il a annoncé que le lycée de Taïba Ndiaye porte désormais officiellement le nom du feu Président Ale Lo, suite à un décret présidentiel pris après validation du ministre de l'Education nationale. De son côté, l'inspecteur Ibrahima Diabaté a salué l'effort de la collectivité, tout en relevant que le taux de réussite de la commune reste en deçà de celui de l'Inspection de l'Education et de la Formation (IEF) de Tivaouane, estimé à 89%, lui-même inférieur à celui de l'Académie de Thiès (93%). « Vous ne devez pas avoir un taux en dessous du taux de l'IEF de Tivaouane, d'autant que vous bénéficiez de l'accompagnement de la mairie et du Parc éolien », a-t-il lancé aux directeurs d'école, annonçant un « encadrement très rapproché » pour cette année scolaire. Il a fixé comme objectif à son district de hisser Taïba Ndiaye à la première place de l'IEF. Ibrahima NDIAYE (Correspondant)

items.title: Le Projet d’Appui au Secteur de la Santé recrute un consultant pour son audit financier et comptable
items.description: NOM DU PROJET : Projet d’Appui au Secteur de la Santé (PASS) SECTEUR: SANTE Modes de financement : Prêt et Vente à Tempérament – Financement Islamique – conforme à la Charia Numéros de financement: Projet GIN 1054 Contexte Le Gouvernement de la République de Guinée a reçu un financement de la Banque Islamique de Développement (BIsD) afin de couvrir le coût du Projet d’Appui au Secteur de la Santé (PASS). A cet effet, un Avis Général de Passation de Marchés (AGPM) a été publié le 30 Juillet 2025. Le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées pour financer les services de consultants. Ces services comprennent le recrutement d’un consultant pour l’audit financier et comptable du projet (exercices 2025-2026, 2027, 2028, 2029 et 2030) sur une base annuelle et un partage des rapports avec le Gouvernement guinéen et la Banque Islamique de Développement pour une période de réalisation de cinq (5) exercices d’audit. Une mission initiale limitée à trois (3) exercices sera envisagée avec possibilité de renouvellement, le cas échéant. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PASS du Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique invite les Consultants éligibles à présenter leur candidature en vue de fournir lesdits services. Les Termes de Référence (TDR) détaillés de la mission sont disponibles au siège du projet à l’adresse ci-dessous indiquée (prière d’utiliser simultanément les deux adresses mail mentionnées) et seront mis à disposition à la demande. A travers une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt, qui constitue une condition de participation à la procédure, les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des renseignements spécifiques démontrant qu’ils sont pleinement qualifiés pour réaliser les prestations (documentation, référence de prestations similaires, expérience dans des conditions comparables, etc.). Pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte le projet sera regardant des critères suivants : Expérience générale : Le Consultant doit être un Cabinet d’Audit et d’Expertise Comptable indépendant, faisant profession habituelle de réviser les comptes, régulièrement inscrit au Tableau d’un Ordre des Experts-comptables reconnus sur le plan international par l’IFAC ou la FIDEF, ayant une expérience confirmée d’au moins dix (10) ans en audit financier et comptable. Les documents de preuve doivent être joints (page de garde et de signature des contrats cités en référence ainsi que les attestations de services faits).Le projet se réservera le droit de vérifier l’authenticité des documents produits. Expérience spécifique : Avoir réalisé au moins cinq (5) missions l’audit de projets/programmes de développement financés par les bailleurs de fonds internationaux (BIsD, BAD, IDA, AFD, FSD, UE etc.). Les attestations de services faits doivent être jointes. Le fait d’avoir réalisé au moins deux (02) missions d’audit financier de projets financés par la Banque Islamique de Développement/BIsD au cours des cinq dernières années (2021-2025) constituera un atout. Capacité : Le consultant doit rassurer sur son statut en présentant les documents administratifs (RCCM, agrément, statuts) ou tout autre document légal justifiant son appartenance au domaine d’activité recherché. Il doit indiquer son organisation technique et managériale ainsi que ses capacités institutionnelles pour mieux conduire la mission. Le Personnel-clé ne fera pas l’objet d’évaluation au stade de l’établissement de la liste retreinte. Une liste restreinte locale d’au plus six (6) bureaux/groupements de bureaux suivant les critères d’évaluation ci-dessus énumérés sera établie à l’issu de l’évaluation du présent Avis à Manifestation d’Intérêt. Les Consultants intéressés sont invités à prendre connaissance des paragraphes 1.12.1 et 1.12.2 des « Politiques des Acquisitions -Directives pour l’Acquisition de Services de Consultants dans le cadre du Financement de Projets par la Banque Islamique de Développement » (les « Directives ») définissant les règles de la BIsD concernant les conflits d’intérêt. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes afin de renforcer leurs qualifications en indiquant clairement le type d’association, c’est-à-dire un groupement de consultants, ou une intention de sous-traitance. Dans le cas de groupement, tous les partenaires du groupement seront conjointement et solidairement responsables pour la totalité du contrat, en cas d’attribution. La sélection se fera en conformité avec la méthode Sélection basée sur le Moindre Coût (SMC) stipulée dans les Directives pour l’Acquisition de Services de Consultant dans le cadre du Financement de projets par la BIsD, édition d’avril 2019, révisée en février 2023. Les consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations additionnelles à l'adresse mentionnée ci-dessous aux heures d’ouverture de bureaux indiquées : 09H00 à 17 H 00, heure locale : COORDINATION NATIONALE DU PROJET D’APPUI AU SECTEUR DE LA SANTE (PASS) Ministère de la Santé, Boulevard du commerce, BP : 585, Conakry, République de Guinée. Siege UGP : Quartier Dixinn – Enceinte Pharmacie Centrale de Guinée (PCG) « Pharmaguinée » Commune de Dixinn Ville : Conakry ; Code postal : 585 ; Pays : République de Guinée Numéro de téléphone : (+224) 622 40 09 40 / 623 61 36 12 Adresse électronique : robertcondeh66@gmail.com / bousoum@yahoo.fr Les manifestations d'intérêt sous forme écrite doivent être physiquement déposées, à l'adresse mentionnée ci-dessus au plus tard le 21 Octobre 2026 à 10H30mn GMT. items.title: Bono East Minister cracks whip on contractors over delayed 24-Hour Economy Market projects
items.description: The Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, has moved swiftly to address delays in the construction of the government’s flagship 24-Hour Economy Market projects, convening a high-stakes review meeting at the Regional Coordinating Council just two weeks after completing a region-wide inspection tour. The meeting, held on Tuesday, brought together all contractors, consultants, engineers, and Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) from the 11 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies across the region. During his recent tour of the region, the Minister inspected ongoing works at each project site. While he expressed satisfaction with the progress of work in some districts, he was visibly disappointed by the performance of some contractors in other areas. The tour, according to the Minister, provided crucial insight into the actual state of the projects on the ground, paving the way for today’s accountability meeting. Speaking at the review meeting, Mr. Owusu Antwi explained that the gathering was designed to achieve multiple objectives. “The meeting seeks to, among other things, assess the progress of work across all 11 Assemblies and identify ways to address delays and improve the performance of contractors who are lagging behind,” he stated. He added that the tour had been instrumental in shaping the discussions. “The tour has helped a lot, and this meeting will also help ensure that this important project is completed on time.” In an unusual move aimed at promoting transparency and accountability, all contractors at the meeting were required to display their work progress and outline the challenges they are facing. The approach appears to have struck a chord with local leaders. The Municipal Chief Executive for Kintampo North, Isaac Donkor, who doubles as the dean of MMDCEs, described the meeting as timely and highly beneficial. “This meeting, which had all contractors display their works and their challenges, was timely and very helpful,” he said. He noted that the open display of progress would foster healthy competition among contractors. “This will create a sort of competition between the contractors who are not doing well to up their game,” Mr. Donkor added. The Regional Minister used the occasion to underscore the broader economic importance of the 24-Hour Economy Market projects. He emphasised that the markets would play a critical role in job creation across the region, while also providing a significant boost to revenue mobilisation efforts of the local assemblies. The government’s 24-Hour Economy initiative is a key policy aimed at stimulating economic activity beyond traditional working hours, creating employment opportunities and enhancing local economic development. With contractors now under pressure to accelerate their work, the Regional Coordinating Council is expected to maintain close monitoring of all project sites. The Minister’s decisive action signals the government’s commitment to ensuring that the flagship projects are delivered on schedule, and that contractors who fail to perform will be held accountable. Residents across the Bono East Region will be watching closely, hopeful that the markets will soon become a reality that transforms their local economies.

items.description: The Pakistan Navy seized narcotics worth approximately $96 million during two successful counter-narcotics operations while deployed in the Arabian Sea, the military’s media wing said on Wednesday. In a press release, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said Pakistan Navy Ship Yarmook conducted the operations “at extended ranges from [the] Pakistani coast, resulting in [the] successful seizure of a large cache of narcotics”. “During the operations, two dhows were intercepted, and approximately 850 kilogrammes of ice and 2,000kg of hashish/cannabis were recovered from concealed compartments inside the vessels,” it said. The seized narcotics, valued at approximately $96m, were taken into custody and will subsequently be handed over to the authorities concerned for further disposal and legal proceedings, according to ISPR. “The successful operations reflect the Pakistan Navy’s sustained presence, vigilance and commitment to regional maritime security and the fight against illicit trafficking at sea,” the statement concluded. President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the Pakistan Navy for its successful counter-narcotics operations in the Arabian Sea. In a statement, he said that the “navy’s role in preventing illegal activities within the country’s maritime boundaries and safeguarding regional maritime security was commendable”. He commended the navy’s continuous vigilance, readiness and resolve against illicit drug smuggling at sea. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also paid tribute to Pakistan Navy for its “successful and timely” operations. In a statement, he said the navy’s role in regional maritime security and in preventing illegal activities at sea was commendable. Last month, the Pakistan Navy seized narcotics worth approximately $750m during a joint counter-narcotics operation in the Arabian Sea. The operation was conducted by Pakistan Navy ships Hunain and Yarmook under the ambit of maritime security operations. In June, the navy seized around two tonnes of drugs — 1,500kg of hashish and 500kg of ice — near the coastline of Gwadar. The value of seized drugs was estimated at around $215m in the international market. In October last year, the navy seized narcotics worth more than $972 m from sailboats in the Arabian Sea.

items.title: PPP stalwart Farooq Naek resigns from Judicial Commission of Pakistan
items.description: ISLAMABAD: PPP stalwart Farooq H. Naek has resigned from the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) — a constitutional body which appoints judges in the superior judiciary. “Yes, I have resigned from the body [due to] personal commitments,” the senator, who has also served as chairman of the upper house of Parliament, told Dawn . In a one-page letter addressed to Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gilani, as well as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, who is the leader of the house in the Senate, Naek expressed gratitude at being appointed a member of the JCP from the treasury benches. He said that it was a “great honour and privilege” for him to serve as a member of the JCP. Naek had participated in a number of JCP proceedings to appoint judges for different high courts as well as the Supreme Court. As a lawyer, he represented PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari before the SC in the presidential reference moved by the latter’s father, President Asif Ali Zardari, in the murder case of former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. He also appeared in several constitutional petitions before the SC, including cases concerning reserved seats, amendments to the accountability laws, presidential immunities and provincial assembly disputes. Although he remained associated with the PPP for three decades, he shot to prominence when he defended late former prime minister Benazir Bhutto and Zardari in a number of corruption and criminal cases during former military dictator Pervez Musharraf’s rule. As a law minister , he also defended the then-federal government in the infamous graft case against Zardari, but eventually dispatched a letter to Swiss Legal authorities in line with SC directions in the National Reconciliation Order case in November 2012 to reopen the case. Naek has served as a senator from Sindh since 2003. He was appointed the law minister after the 2008 general elections, and reappointed in April 2012 after his three-year term as Senate chairman.

items.title: Burkina: du champ au marché, le pays accélère la consolidation de sa souveraineté alimentaire
items.description: À l’occasion de la 3ᵉ édition des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC), le Camarade Ministre d’État, Ministre de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le Commandant Ismaël SOMBIÉ, a animé, ce mardi 6 octobre 2026 au Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), un panel de haut niveau consacré au thème : « Du champ au marché : produire et consommer burkinabè pour renforcer notre souveraineté ». Le panel s’est tenu en présence du Camarade Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel OUEDRAOGO, ainsi que de plusieurs membres du Gouvernement. De la dépendance à la production nationale Dans sa communication introductive, le Ministre d’État a rappelé le paradoxe auquel le Burkina Faso était confronté avant le lancement de l’« Offensive agropastorale et halieutique 2023-2025 ». En 2022, alors que le pays disposait d’importantes potentialités agricoles, hydrauliques et pastorales, près de 19,2 % de la population était en situation de sous-alimentation et le pays consacrait 148,5 milliards de FCFA à l’importation de riz et de blé. Pour le Gouvernement, l’enjeu était donc clair : transformer les terres, l’eau et le potentiel productif du pays en production, en revenus, en emplois et en souveraineté alimentaire. Sur instruction du Camarade Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, l’« Offensive agropastorale et halieutique 2023-2025 » a ainsi été engagée autour d’un objectif central : nourrir le peuple burkinabè par sa propre production, réduire la dépendance extérieure et préserver les devises nationales. 2023-2025 : des résultats qui changent l’échelle de production Les résultats présentés au panel témoignent d’une progression majeure de la production nationale. La production céréalière est passée de 4,66 millions de tonnes avant l’Offensive à 7,14 millions de tonnes en 2025, soit une hausse de 53 %, permettant de couvrir 124 % des besoins céréaliers nationaux. Le riz paddy a franchi, pour la première fois, le seuil symbolique du million de tonnes, avec 1 008 737 tonnes produites en 2025. Le maïs a atteint 2 686 531 tonnes, tandis que la production avicole s’est établie à 18,26 millions de têtes. Ces performances ont été soutenues par d’importants investissements dans l’eau, les aménagements, la mécanisation, les intrants et la santé animale : 11 774 hectares de périmètres irrigués aménagés, 41 275 hectares de bas-fonds aménagés, 120 158 hectares labourés, ainsi que la mise à disposition de centaines de matériels agricoles et de grandes quantités d’engrais et de semences. Le ministre d'Etat, ministre en charge de l'Agriculture, le commandant Ismaël Sombié Produire, mais aussi garantir des débouchés Le panel a également mis en lumière un enjeu déterminant : la souveraineté ne s’arrête pas au champ. Pour que l’augmentation de la production profite directement aux producteurs, le Gouvernement a renforcé la collecte bord champ à travers la transformation de la SONAGESS en centrale d’achats. Plus de 350 000 tonnes de céréales ont ainsi été achetées auprès des producteurs au cours de la campagne 2025-2026. Les stocks de souveraineté alimentaire dépassent désormais 380 000 tonnes. Cette politique permet à la fois de garantir des débouchés aux producteurs, de renforcer les stocks nationaux et de mieux réguler les marchés, notamment pendant les périodes de soudure. De la production à la transformation L’ambition est désormais de franchir un nouveau cap : transformer davantage la production nationale et créer plus de de valeur au Burkina Faso. La dynamique engagée repose sur le développement des infrastructures de stockage et de transformation, avec notamment 418 magasins de stockage, 11 chambres froides, une unité de surgélation de poisson, 63 unités de transformation et 398 kits d’étuvage du riz. L’objectif est de construire une chaîne de valeur complète : produire, collecter, stocker, transformer et consommer burkinabè. 2026-2028 : consolider les acquis et accélérer la cadence Le Ministre d’État a également présenté les grandes orientations de la deuxième phase de l’« Offensive agropastorale et halieutique 2026-2028 ». Dotée d’un coût global de 839,99 milliards de FCFA, dont 85,7 % déjà acquis, cette nouvelle phase entend consolider les acquis tout en renforçant la résilience du pays face aux changements climatiques. Elle cible notamment 20 filières, avec l’ambition de couvrir durablement au moins 120 % des besoins céréaliers nationaux. La maîtrise de l’eau demeure au cœur de cette stratégie, avec 5 nouveaux barrages stratégiques, 200 barrages à réhabiliter ou curer, 100 000 hectares de bas-fonds et 50 000 hectares de périmètres irrigués à réaliser. La souveraineté passera également par des intrants produits davantage au Burkina Faso, avec notamment 177 000 tonnes d’engrais issus du phosphate de Kodjari, mais aussi par la diversification des productions, le développement des agropoles et le renforcement des capacités de stockage et de transformation. Une vue des membres du gouvernement lors du passage du ministre de l'Agriculture « Du champ au marché » : une responsabilité collective En définitive, le message porté par le panel est sans équivoque : la souveraineté alimentaire se construit sur toute la chaîne de valeur. Elle commence par le producteur qui met en valeur la terre, se poursuit avec la collecte et la transformation, et s’accomplit lorsque les Burkinabè choisissent de consommer les produits issus de leur propre travail. Produire davantage. Collecter mieux. Transformer plus. Consommer burkinabè C’est cette chaîne de solidarité économique et patriotique que le Burkina Faso entend consolider pour faire de sa production nationale une source durable de revenus pour les producteurs, de matières premières pour les industries, d’emplois pour la jeunesse et de souveraineté alimentaire pour la Nation. DCRP/MAERAH L’article Burkina: du champ au marché, le pays accélère la consolidation de sa souveraineté alimentaire est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Zelensky condemns ‘vile’ large-scale Russian attacks that killed 15
items.description: At least 15 people have died in overnight strikes across central and eastern Ukraine, in what Volodymyr Zelensky has described as one of Russia’s “most vile” attacks. Ukraine’s president said a residential building in Pryluky in the Chernihiv region was destroyed as a “birthday ‘gift’ to Putin”, who turns 74 on Wednesday. Strikes also hit Kyiv, Dnipro, Kremenchuk, Zaporizhzhia and Oleksandriya. Zelensky said Ukraine had struck targets in attacks on Russia’s Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions in the past 24 hours, adding there was “also a response in the Black Sea”, without providing further details. Moscow is yet to comment on the latest strikes. “The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively,” Zelensky said, adding that 70 missiles were fired in total. In the social media post on Wednesday morning, Zelensky said five people had been killed and 26, including five children, injured in a strike on a five-storey apartment building in Pryluky. He added that people could still be trapped in the rubble. Chernihiv Oblast police later reported that the death toll had risen to nine after the bodies of three children were recovered, with emergency workers continuing a search operation. Two people were also killed and eight injured after Russian missile strikes damaged five apartment buildings in Dnipro and four high-rise buildings in Kremenchuk, said Zelensky. Two people were also killed in the capital, Kyiv, and two others in Oleksandriya, he added. Ukraine’s national police posted pictures online showing what it says is an unexploded Russian Iskander missile in the middle of a Kyiv district. BBC Verify has confirmed the images are genuine and the apparent missile fragments came down in an area of open land surrounded by high-rise apartment buildings. A video posted by the police shows people digging through collapsed remains of a residential building in Pryluky. Another verified video shows damage to cars and what appears to be rubble and a fallen tree in an area surrounded by apartment blocks in Kremenchuk. Zelensky renewed a call for allies to provide air defence support packages to Ukraine, saying its military only managed to shoot down “some” of the missiles launched by Russia overnight. According to Zelensky, one of the “key targets” of the attack was the country’s energy infrastructure, which Moscow earlier said it would intensify strikes on following Ukraine’s strikes on Moscow’s energy facilities. In a separate post on Wednesday, Zelensky said Ukraine had struck four targets in retaliatory attacks in the past 24 hours, including two oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions. “There is also a response in the Black Sea,” the Ukrainian president wrote. On Tuesday evening, footage emerged showing a huge plume of smoke engulfing an oil tanker off the coast of Sochi, along the Black Sea in southern Russia. The Russian transport ministry later said unmanned boats had attacked the Liberian-flagged Aframax Rio oil tanker. Authorities claim the crew was rescued. Separately, Bulgaria has halted a search for the missing crew of a ship that sank after being hit by a drone on Tuesday, Vice-Admiral Rumen Nikolov from the Maritime Administration Executive Agency said, as reported by Bulgarian television network Nora TV. Tracking data shows the ship was anchored at the southern end of the Bosphorus strait until Monday when it entered the Black Sea heading north. Its last reported position on ship-tracking site MarineTraffic was at 23:43 GMT on Monday in what is known as the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone of the Black Sea. Bulgarian specialist news outlet Maritime.bg reported the Alfa Watan was attacked by a drone and sank 70nm (130km) east of Byala. As well as the civilian cargo ship, a second vessel – carrying grain – was also hit within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, its Prime Minister Rumen Radev said on Tuesday. The 18 crew members on the second vessel were rescued. Bulgaria has not said who it believes was behind the attacks. It comes as Russia intensifies strikes in the Black Sea, particularly the eastern side, as part of its war against Ukraine. In an evening address on Tuesday, Zelensky claimed Russia was responsible for the attacks. Moscow has not commented on the latest incident.
